topics.title: Home
topics.body:
Welcome to **SquatClient**, a graphical client for MUDs, MUSHes and other MU* games. It remembers your worlds, keeps full-colour scrollback, lets you automate things with a TinyFugue-style scripting language or Lua, and can keep your connections alive while the app is closed.

This help is built into the app. It works offline and everything in it is searchable.

## Where to start

- New here? Read [Getting started](help:getting-started).
- Want to connect to a game? See [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting).
- Want your connections to survive closing the app? See [Squatter](help:squatter).
- Looking for a key? See [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys).
- Something not working? See [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).
- Want to automate things with triggers and macros? Start with [the scripting language](help:scripting), then [Lua scripting](help:lua).
- Unsure what a word means? See the [Glossary](help:glossary).

## All topics

- [Getting started](help:getting-started): first launch, quick connect, your first commands.
- [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting): saved worlds, encryption, logins, passwords.
- [Squatter](help:squatter): connections that keep running while the app is closed.
- [Using the client](help:using): output, scrollback, the input line, history, tabs, themes, colours.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys)
- [Settings reference](help:settings)
- [Commands](help:commands): everything you can type that starts with `/`.
- [The scripting language](help:scripting): macros, triggers, expressions, hooks.
- [Lua scripting](help:lua): the `squat` functions for larger plugins.
- [TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat): how the scripting language compares with TinyFugue.
- [What's new](help:whats-new), [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting), [Glossary](help:glossary)
- [About and credits](help:about)

## Using this help

| To do this             | Do this                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open help              | type `/help`, press F1 (Cmd-? on macOS), choose Help in the menu, or click the **?** button                                 |
| Open a topic           | `/help def`, `/help keys`, `/help squatter` (a leading `/` is fine: `/help /def`)                                           |
| Search                 | type in the search box, or `/help some words`                                                                               |
| Move around            | click the topic tree, follow links, or press Alt-Left and Alt-Right for back and forward                                    |
| Jump to the search box | press `/`                                                                                                                   |
| Close                  | press Escape                                                                                                                |
| Try an example         | every code block has **Copy** and **Insert into input** buttons; Insert puts the text on your input line without sending it |

SquatClient's scripting language is modelled on [TinyFugue](help:about#tinyfugue), written by Ken Keys. Thank you, Ken.

topics.title: Getting started
topics.body:
This page takes you from a fresh install to your first connection.

## First launch

When SquatClient starts with no connection open you see an empty window with two buttons:

- **Worlds** opens the world manager, where your saved connections live.
- **Quick connect** connects to a host and port without saving anything.

Once you connect, the window has a tab bar on top (one tab per connection), the output pane in the middle, one input line below it and a status bar at the bottom.

## Quick connect

1. Click **Quick connect** (or press Cmd-N on macOS, Ctrl-N elsewhere).
2. Enter the **Host** and **Port**. A good game to try is `startrekkin.net` on port `1701`.
3. Tick **Use TLS** only if the game offers an encrypted port.
4. Press **Connect**.

A new tab opens and the game's greeting appears. Type into the input line and press Enter to send what you typed to the game.

## Save a world

A **world** is a saved connection. It remembers the host, port, encryption, text encoding and an optional login so you can reconnect with a double-click.

1. Open the world manager with Ctrl-O (Cmd-O on macOS) or the button in the tab bar.
2. Add a world and fill in the details; see [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting).
3. Double-click the world to connect.

## Your first commands

Anything you type is sent to the game, except lines that start with `/`. Those are **commands** to SquatClient itself.

| Type          | What happens                                                                              |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/help`       | opens this help                                                                           |
| `/help keys`  | opens a topic; any word works                                                             |
| `/echo Hello` | prints a note on your screen (nothing is sent to the game)                                |
| `/colortest`  | prints a colour chart; see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#colours-look-different) |

The full list is in [Commands](help:commands).

## Things to try next

- Scroll up with PageUp. Output pauses while you read and **--More--** shows in the status bar. Press End to return to live output. See [Using the client](help:using#scrollback-and-pausing).
- Search the output with Cmd-F (Ctrl-Shift-F elsewhere).
- Press Up to bring back lines you sent earlier, or Ctrl-R to search all of them.
- Try your first trigger. This highlights every line with "dragon" in it:

```
/def -t'*dragon*' -ahC#ff4040 dragon
```

## Where to find help

- Press F1 or type `/help` at any time.
- Type `/help` followed by a command name to read about it, for example `/help def`.
- If something misbehaves, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).

## Keeping connections alive

By default a world connects **Direct** and the connection ends when you quit the app. To keep connections running while the app is closed, set up a squatter and choose it in a world's **Connect via** setting; see [Squatter](help:squatter).

## What next

Read [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting) to set up your games, then [Using the client](help:using) to learn the input line.

topics.title: Squatters and routing
topics.body:
## The model

- A **squatter** is a saved remote relay: a `squatterd` you run on a server, or a TinyFugue ([TinyFugue as a squatter](help:squatter/tinyfugue)). You can save **many** squatters, for example `home-vps` and `work-box`.
- Each **world** chooses how it connects with its **Connect via** setting:
  - **Direct**: straight from this computer to the game. The connection ends when the app closes.
  - **A saved squatter**: the squatter holds the game connection. It survives closing the app, and when you come back everything you missed is replayed.
- Different worlds can use different squatters, and some can be direct, all at the same time.
- There is **one hop** for now: SquatClient, then the squatter, then the game. Chaining squatters, or a squatter that goes out through a proxy, is not available yet.

## Example

| World      | Connect via | What happens                                 |
| ---------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Star Trek  | home-vps    | held by `home-vps`; still connected tomorrow |
| Work MUSH  | work-box    | held by `work-box`                           |
| Quick test | Direct      | ends when you quit                           |

## Adding a squatter

1. On the server run `./squatterd --port 10327`.
2. On the server run `./squatterd pair` and note the one-time code and the fingerprint.
3. In SquatClient open the squatters dialog, choose **Add a squatter**, and enter the name, host, port and code.
4. Check that the fingerprint shown matches the one `squatterd pair` printed, then press **Trust and pair**.
5. In each world that should use it, set **Connect via** to the new squatter.

The longer story is in [Squatter](help:squatter).

### When the port is firewalled

If you cannot reach the server's port directly, use Tailscale (enter the server's Tailscale address as the host) or an ssh tunnel:

```
ssh -N -L 10327:127.0.0.1:10327 user@server
```

Then add the squatter in SquatClient as host `127.0.0.1`, port `10327`. On the server, start squatterd with `--bind 127.0.0.1 --insecure-loopback`: it then accepts only connections from the server itself, which is safe because the ssh tunnel already encrypts everything.

## Detaching and ended sessions

`/suspend` and `/detach` let go of the squatter sessions; they keep running. An ended session is just history: nothing reconnects by itself, and the squatter stores no game passwords. See [Squatter](help:squatter#suspend-and-detach).

## What next

If a squatter will not connect, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#lost-squatter-connection).

topics.title: Connecting and worlds
topics.body:
A **world** is a saved connection to a game. Open the world manager with Ctrl-O (Cmd-O on macOS), the menu (Session, Worlds) or the button in the tab bar. Select a world and press **Connect**, or double-click it. Worlds are stored in your SquatClient configuration folder. Passwords are not: they go to your operating system's keychain.

## World fields

| Field                         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name                          | what the tab shows                                                                                                                                                  |
| Group                         | optional folder name used to group the list                                                                                                                         |
| Host and Port                 | where the game listens                                                                                                                                              |
| Connect via                   | **Direct** (from this computer; ends when the app closes) or a saved squatter that holds the connection for you; see [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing) |
| Encoding                      | how text from the game is decoded: UTF-8 (default) or Latin-1                                                                                                       |
| Use TLS                       | encrypt the connection                                                                                                                                              |
| Skip certificate verification | accept any certificate; only for games with a self-signed certificate                                                                                               |
| Connect automatically         | connect when the app starts                                                                                                                                         |
| Login template                | text sent after connecting; `{name}` and `{password}` are filled in for you                                                                                         |
| Character name                | replaces `{name}`                                                                                                                                                   |
| Password                      | replaces `{password}`; stored in the OS keychain                                                                                                                    |
| Notes                         | free text for yourself                                                                                                                                              |

## Encryption (TLS)

Tick **Use TLS** when the game offers an encrypted port. Certificates are checked strictly by default. Some games use a self-signed certificate; for those, tick **Skip certificate verification**. That removes the protection against someone impersonating the game, so only use it for games you trust.

## Text encoding

UTF-8 is the default. It handles accented letters, emoji and box-drawing characters. Some older games send Latin-1; if accents look garbled, switch that world to Latin-1. You can set the default for new connections in [Settings](help:settings).

## Login templates

If a world has a login template, SquatClient sends it for you after connecting. A typical MUSH template is:

```
connect {name} {password}
```

## Passwords and the keychain

Game passwords are saved in the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or the Secret Service on Linux), never in the worlds file. The file only records that a password exists. If the keychain cannot be reached, connecting to a world that needs a password fails with an error instead of sending an empty password.

A squatter never stores your game passwords either: your client sends the login every time. Lines that look like logins or password changes are masked on screen and never saved in history; see [Passwords](help:using#passwords).

## Several connections

Each connection is a tab. Press Alt-1 to Alt-9 to switch, or Ctrl-Tab and Ctrl-Shift-Tab to cycle. A badge on a tab counts unread lines in background connections, and the status bar shows how many are active. Closing a tab disconnects it. A connection that has ended stays in its tab until you dismiss it, showing the reason and the last text received.

## Worlds from scripts

Scripts can also define and connect worlds; see `/addworld`, `/connect`, `/world` and `/fg` in [Commands](help:commands).

## What next

To keep a connection running while the app is closed, read [Squatter](help:squatter). If a connection fails, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#cannot-connect).

topics.title: TinyFugue as a squatter
topics.body:
If you already run **TinyFugue** (TF) on a server, it can act as your squatter. You see all of its connections in SquatClient, read their history and type into them, while TinyFugue keeps running its own triggers and macros.

## Setting it up

1. In TinyFugue (built with the squat support) run `/squat start`, then `/squat pair`. It prints a one-time **pairing code** and its **fingerprint**.
2. In SquatClient open the Squatters dialog, choose **Add a squatter**, set **Type** to **TinyFugue**, and enter the host, the port (10328 unless you changed it) and the code.
3. Compare the fingerprint, then press **Trust and pair**.

A TinyFugue squatter and a `squatterd` use different ports and different protocol paths. If you pick the wrong Type, SquatClient says so and nothing is sent to the server.

## Who has the keyboard

Every TinyFugue connection shows a badge on its tab and a **Keyboard** control in the status bar:

| Choice                | Keyboard         | Triggers and macros |
| --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------- |
| **Watch only**        | TinyFugue        | TinyFugue           |
| **Type too**          | both of you      | TinyFugue           |
| **Take the keyboard** | only SquatClient | TinyFugue           |
| **Take over fully**   | only SquatClient | SquatClient         |

While TinyFugue keeps the keyboard, the input line is disabled and says so. If TinyFugue is set to ask first (`squat_takeover=ask`), the change waits until its user allows it and you see a message meanwhile.

Triggers run in only one place at a time, so nothing fires twice. By default TinyFugue runs them and SquatClient only shows the result. In the Squatters dialog you can choose **this app (while connected)**: SquatClient then takes over triggers whenever it is connected and TinyFugue gets them back when you leave.

Lines you did not type are marked in the output: `[tf]` for TinyFugue's own keyboard and `[remote]` for another device.

## TinyFugue's worlds

Press **Worlds…** next to a TinyFugue squatter to see, add, edit, delete and connect TinyFugue's own world records. Passwords are write-only: they are stored in TinyFugue and never shown or kept by SquatClient. TinyFugue logs in by itself, so SquatClient sends nothing for the login. A **viewer** device can look and connect but not edit.

## Sending scripts to TinyFugue

Press **Scripts…** (admin devices) to send a TinyFugue macro file to TinyFugue and activate it there: pick a file or paste the text, name it (letters, digits, `.` `_` `-`, ending in `.tf`) and press **Send and load**. Sending the same name again replaces the script and loads it again.

What the script may do is decided in TinyFugue, by `squat_scripts`:

| Setting       | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| off (default) | uploads are refused                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `safe`        | the script runs **sandboxed**: no shell (`/sh`, `/quote !`), no files, no new connections, no Lua, and it cannot change TinyFugue's `squat_` settings or its restriction level. The same holds whenever one of its triggers or macros fires later |
| `on`          | the script runs with TinyFugue's own rights, like a file you loaded yourself                                                                                                                                                                      |

Use `safe` unless you wrote the script. Deleting a script removes only the file: triggers it already defined stay until you undefine them or TinyFugue restarts.

## Gagged lines

Lines TinyFugue gagged are hidden by default. **Settings → Show lines TinyFugue gagged** shows them, marked as gagged.

## GMCP and MSDP

GMCP and MSDP data from games reaches SquatClient too, and you can send GMCP or MSDP requests to a game through TinyFugue.

## Limits

- What SquatClient may do depends on the role the pairing gave this device (viewer, operator or admin). Running a TinyFugue command or sending a script needs admin, and TinyFugue's `squat_exec` / `squat_scripts` settings must allow it.
- Everything is held by TinyFugue: if it exits, its sessions end.

topics.title: Squatter
topics.body:
A **squatter** keeps your game connections running while SquatClient is closed. It is a small separate program, `squatterd`, that you run on a computer that stays on, such as a home server or a cheap virtual server. Think of `screen` or TinyFugue on a shell account.

Already using TinyFugue on a server? It can be your squatter too: see [TinyFugue as a squatter](help:squatter/tinyfugue).

## Why use one

- You close the app, and the game never notices: you stay logged in.
- The squatter keeps recording what the game says. When you open SquatClient again it replays everything you missed and carries on live.
- You can attach from different computers.

You do not need a squatter to use SquatClient. Without one, connections are **direct** and end when you quit the app.

What a squatter does **not** do:

- It **never logs in for you** and **stores no game passwords**. SquatClient sends the login lines each time.
- It **never reconnects to a game by itself**. If the game closes the connection, the session is shown as ended, with the reason, until you dismiss it.
- **SquatClient does reconnect to the squatter by itself.** If your laptop sleeps or the network drops, the squatter keeps your games connected; the app reconnects to it a moment after the network is back (or the window is shown again) and catches up on everything you missed. You can turn this off in [Settings](help:settings), and the Squatters dialog has a Reconnect button to do it right away.

## Setting it up

You need two things: `squatterd` running on the server, and SquatClient paired with it. Pairing happens once per computer.

1. Get `squatterd` for the server from <https://github.com/itsnotyoutoday/squatClientDaemon> and start it there:

   ```
   ./squatterd --port 10327
   ```

   The default port is 10327, connections to it are encrypted, and its files live in `~/.squatterd`. Run `./squatterd --help` for the other options, for example `--bind` to limit the address it listens on and `--data-dir` to move its files.

2. On the server, in a second terminal, run:

   ```
   ./squatterd pair
   ```

   It prints a one-time **pairing code** such as `ABCD-EFGH` (valid for ten minutes), the server's **fingerprint**, and a host and port hint.

3. In SquatClient open the squatters dialog (the tab-bar button), choose **Add a squatter**, and enter a name, the host, the port (10327 unless you changed it) and the pairing code. Press **Pair**.

4. Compare the fingerprint SquatClient shows with the one `squatterd pair` printed. If they are the same, press **Trust and pair**. If they differ, press **Reject**: something is between you and your server.

5. In the world manager set a world's **Connect via** to your squatter. See [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing).

## The fingerprint check

The squatter makes its own encryption certificate, so no outside authority vouches for it. SquatClient therefore asks you to confirm the fingerprint once, and from then on it only talks to a server with exactly that fingerprint. If the fingerprint ever changes, the connection is refused.

Only pair computers you trust: anyone who can pair can open connections to any game from the server. `./squatterd revoke <deviceId>` removes a paired computer.

## Leaving and coming back

### /suspend and /detach

Type `/suspend` (or `/detach`) to let go of your squatter sessions while leaving them running. SquatClient lets go of them, the window is minimised, and the sessions keep recording. To come back choose **Resume** in the Session menu (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-R); everything you missed is replayed. Closing the app has the same effect for squatter sessions.

Direct connections cannot outlive the app, so `/suspend` leaves them connected and just minimises the window. If you have both kinds open, only the squatter sessions are detached.

### Ended sessions

When a game closes the connection, resets it or cannot be reached, the session is **ended**. The tab shows the reason, the time and the last text received, and the history is kept. Choose **Connect again** to open a fresh connection, or **Dismiss** to remove the tab. Nothing reconnects by itself.

## Security summary

- Connections to the squatter are encrypted, and the certificate is pinned when you pair.
- Your computer proves who it is with a key; the squatter remembers only the public half.
- Pairing codes work once and expire. Repeated wrong codes lock the sender out for five minutes.
- If the squatter's port is not reachable, see [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing#when-the-port-is-firewalled).

## What next

Read [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing) to use several squatters, or [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#lost-squatter-connection) if a squatter does not respond.

topics.title: Using the client
topics.body:
## The window

- **Tab bar**: one tab per connection, plus buttons for worlds, quick connect, squatters, search, settings and help.
- **Output pane**: what the game says, plus your own typed lines and system messages.
- **Input line**: where you type. Lines starting with `/` are commands, anything else is sent to the game.
- **Status bar**: connection state, activity in other tabs, the pause marker, any fields your scripts add, and the clock.

## Output pane

Text keeps the colours and styles the game sends: bold, dim, italic, underline, strikethrough, blink and reverse. Colours can be the 16 theme colours, the 256-colour xterm palette, or 24-bit truecolour, and all of UTF-8 is displayed. Links the game marks up, and bare `http://` and `https://` addresses (if enabled in [Settings](help:settings)), are clickable and open in your system browser. Only web addresses are ever opened.

Select text with the mouse and copy it as usual.

## Scrollback and pausing

Recent output is kept in memory, up to the **scrollback lines** setting; older history is fetched on demand when you scroll up. Use PageUp and PageDown to scroll, or the mouse wheel.

When you scroll up, live output **pauses** so the text you are reading does not move (if _Pause output when scrolled up_ is on). The status bar shows **--More--** with a count of lines that arrived meanwhile. Press End (when the output has focus) or the jump button to return to live output. This takes the place of TinyFugue's `--More--` prompt.

## Searching

Press Cmd-F or Ctrl-Shift-F (Ctrl-F when the output has focus) to open the search bar. It offers previous and next match, case sensitivity and regular expressions, and searches the whole scrollback of the current tab.

## Editing the input line

The input line understands the Emacs editing keys TinyFugue users know. The full list is in [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys). Highlights:

- Home/End or Ctrl-A/Ctrl-E move to the start or end.
- Ctrl-W and Alt-D delete words; Ctrl-K and Ctrl-U delete to the end or the whole line; Ctrl-Y pastes the last deletion.
- Shift-Enter inserts a new line so you can write several lines before sending.
- Pasting several lines sends them one by one.
- Escape clears the line.
- Ctrl-R opens the history browser; Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-E switches to the editor.

### History

Up and Down (or Ctrl-P and Ctrl-N) walk through lines you sent earlier. If you typed something first, only lines starting with it are offered, so typing `/def` and pressing Up finds your last `/def` command.

History is kept **per world**, on disk, so it survives restarts and is shared by every tab of the same world. A multi-line block is one entry. Passwords and anything typed while the game has echo off are never stored. How many entries are kept is the _Command history size_ setting (default 20,000; see [Settings](help:settings)).

### History browser

Press Ctrl-R (or Cmd-Shift-H), or click **History** next to the input, to search everything you have sent to this world.

- Type to filter at once. **.\*** switches to regular expressions and **Aa** to case-sensitive matching; matches are highlighted.
- Up and Down select (PageUp, PageDown, Ctrl-Home, Ctrl-End jump), Enter puts the entry into the input (into the editor if it has several lines), Shift-Enter sends it now, Cmd/Ctrl-C copies it, Delete removes it, Escape closes.
- Click selects, double-click loads. **Clear history** asks for confirmation first.

## Resizing the command window

Drag the thin bar above the input upwards to make the command window taller (up to about 70% of the window); the output shrinks to match. Focus the bar and use Up and Down (PageUp and PageDown for five lines, Home for the tallest, End for the smallest). Double-click it to reset. The height is remembered.

## Multi-line mode

For big pieces of code press **Editor** (or Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-E): the input becomes a large **code editor** made for MUSH softcode. It loads the first time you open it.

- It colours softcode as you type (functions, `[ ]` `{ }` `( )`, `%` substitutions, `#dbrefs`, `&ATTR` and `@commands`, `$` patterns, `@@` comments), marks the matching bracket, closes `(` `[` `{` for you and underlines brackets that do not balance (the toolbar counts them).
- Enter inserts a new line; **Cmd/Ctrl-Enter sends the whole buffer**; **Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-Enter** (or the _Send line / selection_ button) sends only the selection, or the line under the cursor together with the indented lines that continue it.
- Tab inserts two spaces (with a selection it indents every selected line); Shift-Tab outdents. Undo and redo (Cmd/Ctrl-Z, Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-Z or Ctrl-Y) work as in any editor. Line numbers, the line and column, and _Wrap_ (off by default) are in the toolbar.
- **Cmd/Ctrl-F searches inside the editor** (with replace); Escape closes that search first. The output search stays on Cmd/Ctrl-F whenever you are not in the editor.
- **Expand** breaks long function calls over indented lines so you can read them, and **Collapse** puts them back; both work on the selection, or on everything when nothing is selected, and Collapse after Expand gives back exactly what you had. Keys: Cmd/Ctrl-Alt-] and Cmd/Ctrl-Alt-[.
- Escape (with no search open) returns to the single line and keeps your text. Unsent text is kept as a **draft** for the world, across tab switches and restarts.
- Pasting several lines in the editor inserts them there instead of sending them.

### Checking brackets before sending

When you send from the editor (the whole buffer, or the selection or line) and the code has brackets that do not balance, a dialog says how many problems there are and on which lines. **Fix first** puts the cursor on the first problem and sends nothing; **Send anyway** sends it as it is. Turn the check off with _Editor: ask before sending unbalanced brackets_ in [Settings](help:settings). Single-line input is never checked.

### Sending blocks

Every resulting line is sent to the game separately, in order:

- **Indented lines continue the previous line** (setting _Editor: join indented lines_, on by default). A line starting with a space or tab has its leading whitespace removed and is appended directly to the line before it, with no space added, so indent freely for readability: `&FN obj=[add(1,` followed by `  2)]` is sent as `&FN obj=[add(1,2)]`. Add a space yourself where the code needs one.
- **Blank lines and lines holding only an `@@` comment are dropped** (setting _Editor: drop blank and @@ comment lines_, on by default), also between a line and its continuation. Trailing spaces are always removed.
- With _Delay between block lines_ above 0 the lines go out one per interval so a big block does not flood the game; a progress bar and a **Cancel** button show while it runs (lines already sent cannot be taken back).

### Passwords

Lines like `connect name password`, `create name password` and `@password ...` are recognised automatically and are never echoed, stored or logged by a squatter; the screen shows them masked (`connect name ********`). Use `/secret text` for anything else you must keep out of logs.

When the game turns off echo (for a password prompt) the input becomes a masked password field with a lock icon, history is disabled and what you type is not recorded.

## Uploading a file

`/upload` sends a text file to the game, for example a softcode installer. Type `/upload` to choose the file in the system file dialog (it starts in the folder you used last; text and code files such as `.txt` `.mush` `.mu` `.tf` `.lua` `.md` are listed first, All Files is one click away), or `/upload ~/code/install.mush` to give the path yourself (`~/` is your home folder; use quotes if the path has spaces). You can also **drag a text file onto the window**. Nothing is sent yet: a dialog opens first.

- The dialog shows the file name, size, line count and a scrollable preview with line numbers (a second tab shows exactly what will be sent). Large files stay responsive.
- It follows the same rules as multi-line mode: _join continuation lines_ and _skip blank and @@ comment lines_ start from your settings, and you can change them for this upload. The number of commands that will be sent is shown. _Delay per line_ starts from your setting, or 50 ms when that is 0, so the game is not flooded; an optional _prefix_ is put in front of every command.
- The commands go to the world shown as **Send to** (the one in front), one line at a time. If the code has unbalanced brackets the first problems are listed and the button reads **Send anyway**.
- While it runs you see a progress bar, the current line and the elapsed time, with **Pause**, **Resume** and **Cancel**. At the end a summary says how many commands were sent and skipped, or where it was cancelled. Closing the dialog while sending cancels the rest.
- Command history gets one entry, `/upload install.mush`, not the whole file.
- Only plain text files up to 5 MiB are accepted (binary files are refused with a message). UTF-8 and Latin-1 files both work; line endings are normalised. The app reads only the file you chose or typed.

## Tabs

Each connection has a tab. Use Alt-1 to Alt-9 or Ctrl-Tab to switch. Unread lines in background tabs show as a badge, and with desktop notifications on you also get notified. The small **x** on a tab disconnects it, or dismisses it if it has already ended.

## Themes

Pick a theme in [Settings](help:settings): **Dark**, **Light** or **High contrast**. A theme sets the text and background colours, the 16 ANSI colours and the colours of the window chrome. You can import your own theme as JSON. If some colour combinations are hard to read, set **Minimum contrast** (4.5 is the WCAG AA level) and the client nudges colours to meet it. The client respects your system's _reduce motion_ preference.

## Colours

By default SquatClient shows UTF-8 text with xterm-256 and 24-bit truecolour. Type `/colortest` to print every colour mode (16 colours, the full 256 grid, truecolor gradients, text styles and UTF-8) and compare it with another program.

**Why basic colours can differ between programs:** colours 0-15 (the plain `red`, `yellow`, ... and their bright versions) are not fixed: every terminal and theme chooses its own shades, and games that use them look different in different clients. Colours 16-255 (xterm-256) and truecolour are exact everywhere. SquatClient's default dark theme uses a classic terminal palette so a game that sends basic colours looks like it does in tinyfugue; if a slot looks wrong, change it in a custom theme (see below). _Bold text uses bright colours_ makes bold text switch to the bright variant of the 8 basic colours, as in many terminals. In scripts you can use all of these colours; see [Attributes](help:scripting/attributes).

## Accessibility

Dialogs trap keyboard focus and close with Escape, controls have labels, and _Screen-reader mode_ announces new lines to assistive technology. A "Skip to input" link is the first thing a keyboard user reaches.

## What next

Learn the keys in [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys), tune the client in [Settings](help:settings), or automate it with [the scripting language](help:scripting). If something looks wrong, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).

topics.title: Editing objects and attributes
topics.body:
The Object Editor lets you work on objects and their attributes in a game as if they were files: a list of attributes on the left, a full code editor on the right, and tabs for every object you have open. It needs a connected world, because it reads and writes through the game itself.

## Which games it is for

The Object Editor is the module for MU* games: PennMUSH, CobraMUSH, TinyMUX, TinyMUSH, TinyMUSE and RhostMUSH. Other kinds of game do not get it: there is no button, Cmd-E does nothing, and `/edit` answers "no such command".

SquatClient finds out what kind of game a world is by itself: it recognises the server's name (or, for Diku-style games, the classic "By what name do you wish to be known?" prompt) in the first lines the game prints, and after you log in it quietly asks the game for its version with `version()` and, if that does not name the server, `@version` (nothing appears in the output). A game that is not logged in yet is not detected yet, so the editor shows up a moment after you connect. If detection gets it wrong, or the game hides its version, set it yourself:

- in the world's settings (Worlds, then **Game type**), which is remembered, or
- with `/gametype pennmush` (or `cobramush`, `tinymux`, `tinymush`, `rhostmush`, `tinymuse`, `mush` for any other MU*) for the current connection. Other kinds of game have types too (`circlemud`, `rom`, `smaug`, `diku`, `lpmud`, `lambdamoo`, `evennia`, `muck`, `coldmud`, `coffeemud`, `ironrealms`, `custom`), and `other` means none of these. They never get the Object Editor. `/gametype` alone shows the current type and `/gametype auto` detects it again.

## Opening the editor

| How                          | What happens                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/edit`                      | open the Object Editor and bring back the objects you had open          |
| `/edit #12`                  | open object #12                                                         |
| `/edit #12/CMD_ENGAGE`       | open object #12 and select the attribute `CMD_ENGAGE`                   |
| `/edit me`, `/edit here`     | open yourself, or the room you are in                                   |
| `/edit Nav Console`          | open an object by name (the game finds it; use a `#dbref` if two match) |
| Cmd-E (Ctrl-E)               | switch between the terminal and the editor                              |
| the **Object Editor** button | the same, from the top bar                                              |

`/edit` is handled by the window itself and is never sent to the game. Your connections keep running while you edit: switch back with Cmd-E, Escape or the **Terminal** button and everything that happened is in the output. Ctrl-E is the end-of-line key on the input line, so there it does not switch views; use Cmd-E, the button, or press Ctrl-E from anywhere else.

## The layout

- **Top row**: the connected worlds. Click one to switch world (Alt-1 to Alt-9 work too). Each world has its own set of open objects.
- **Second row**: the objects open in that world, labelled `Name (#12)`. A dot marks unsaved changes. Close a tab with its x or Cmd-W; drag tabs to reorder. The **+** asks for an object: `#123`, `me`, `here` or a name, optionally followed by `/ATTRIBUTE`.
- **Left**: the attribute list with a filter box. A dot means modified, `!` means the last save was refused, a padlock means read-only, `+` means a new attribute that is not saved yet. **+ new attribute** adds one; it is created by its first save.
- **Right**: the code editor for the selected attribute, with highlighting, bracket matching and a problems list. Every attribute you visit keeps its unsaved text and its undo history while you switch.
- **Bottom strip**: the number of bracket problems, the object's owner, type and flags, whether you control it, and the game's last reply.

## Permissions

When you open an object the client asks the game whether you control it.

- **You do not control it**: the object opens read-only with a notice. You can read, copy and compare, but Save is off and the editor will not accept typing.
- **The game could not say**: you can edit, and a notice says the game will decide when you save.
- **A protected attribute** (locked or safe) shows a padlock and opens read-only when the game reports it as protected. Otherwise the game's reply on save decides.

## Saving safely

Press **Save**, Cmd-S (Ctrl-S), or Cmd-Shift-S to save every changed attribute of the object. Before it writes, the client reads the attribute again.

1. **Someone changed it meanwhile**: nothing is saved, and a dialog shows the game's version and yours side by side. Choose **Overwrite** (store yours), **Reload theirs** (drop your changes) or **Keep editing** (your next save then overwrites).
2. **The game refuses**: your text stays exactly as you typed it, a red notice shows the game's own words (for example `Permission denied.`), and Save stays available.
3. **After a successful save** the value is read back. You see **Saved**, or a warning if the game stored something different from what you sent.

Closing a tab with unsaved changes asks whether to save them, discard them, or keep editing. Unsaved text is also kept between sessions: reopen the editor and it comes back marked as a restored draft. If the attribute changed in the game in the meantime, the same conflict dialog appears when you save.

Nothing the editor reads or writes appears in the output pane or in your command history.

## Formatting and what is sent

Long softcode is easier to read indented. **Expand** and **Collapse** (also Cmd-Alt-] and Cmd-Alt-[) change only how it looks: what is sent to the game is always the collapsed single line, exactly as when you send a block from the command window. They never change what the code means.

**%r as line breaks** shows `%r` as real line breaks and `%t` as tabs, which suits descriptions. Saving turns them back into `%r` and `%t`. While it is on, Expand and Collapse are off, because the line breaks are then part of the text. Attributes the game stored with real line breaks open in this view automatically. A `%` right before a line break cannot be saved safely; write `%%` or remove it, and the client tells you if you try.

**Wrap** wraps long lines. **Compare** shows the game's current value next to yours.

## Object overview header

Across the top of the editor, above whatever you are editing, a compact header always shows the selected object: its name, number, type, owner and location (click the owner or location to open it), then its **Flags**, **Powers** and **Locks** as small chips with their counts (a lock chip reads like `Basic: =#45 | flag^WIZARD`; hover for the full key and the lock's flags). Long groups end in **+N more**, which expands them. Click a chip or a group name to jump to that section of Object details; the **+** next to a group starts adding one. A padlock badge marks an object you cannot change. **Refresh** reads the object again, and the arrow collapses the header to one line (remembered for each world). The header shares one quiet read with Object details and updates after any change you make.

## Object details

The first entry of the left list, **Object details**, shows everything about the object itself instead of one attribute (Cmd-Shift-D). The **Overview** tab has these sections:

- **Identity**: the name (type a new one and press Enter or **Rename**), the number, the type, the owner (**Chown...** gives it to someone else), pennies, created and modified times, the attribute count and, for players, alias, channels and quota when the game tells.
- **Location**: where the object is, with a **Move...** button. For an exit it shows where the exit starts and where it leads.
- **Relations**: parent (with the parents above it), zone and home, each with **Change...** and **Clear**.
- **Flags** and **Powers**: each one set is a chip; the **x** on a chip turns it off. **Add flag** is a box that lists the flags the game offers with a short description; type to narrow the list, use the arrow keys and Enter, or type any name. Hover a chip for its letter and description. Powers work the same way and usually need a wizard.
- **Locks**: every lock the object has (Basic, Enter, Use, Zone, Page, Teleport and more, plus your own `user:name` locks), each with its key, its flags as buttons you can switch on and off (visual, no_inherit, no_clone, wizard, locked), **Edit** and **Clear**. **New lock...** adds one.
- **Warnings**: the object's warning checks, a box to set them, and **Run @wcheck** to see the game's report.
- **Contents** and **Exits**: click an item to open it in a new tab.

Every change shows a spinner on its control, then the state read back from the game. If the game refuses, you see its exact words next to the control, the old value stays, and nothing is lost. When you do not control the object, a notice says so and the controls are off. **Refresh** reads everything again. All of this happens quietly: nothing appears in the output pane or in your command history, and the game's replies show in the strip at the bottom of the view.

### Raw examine

The **Raw examine** tab runs the game's own `examine` for the object and shows its text with colours, so anything the Overview cannot show is still there. Choose Normal, All or Brief, press **Refresh**, or **Copy** the text.

### The lock editor

**Edit** on a lock (or **New lock...**) opens a dialog with the key in a text box and buttons that insert pieces: a number, `=#` (is exactly), `+#` (carries), `@#` (use another object's lock), `flag^`, `type^`, `power^`, an attribute test, and the combinators `&`, `|`, `!` and brackets. The dialog warns when brackets do not balance. **Test** asks the game whether the stored lock lets a chosen object through (`me`, a number or a name); save first to test a change. **Save** sets the lock and reads it back; **Clear lock** removes it.

### Moving an object

**Move...** opens a dialog. Type part of a room name or a number to search, or pick from **Nearby** (where it is now, where the exits of that room lead, and what is there) or **Recently used**. Clicking a place only looks at it: you see its owner, a short description, and its exits, which you can follow. A sentence such as "Move Widget (#123) to Garden (#11)?" says exactly what will happen; **Move** does it and the details refresh. Some games do not let you search every room; the dialog then says so and shows your own rooms and things nearby. **Set home** and the exit's **Change...** use the same dialog.

## Attribute menu

Right-click an attribute in the list (or press Shift-F10, the Menu key or F while the list has focus, or use the **...** button above the editor) for its menu:

- **Flags** with check marks: no_command, no_inherit, no_clone, mortal_dark, wizard, veiled, case, nearby, locked, safe, visual, regexp. Pick one to switch it; the game's reply shows if it refuses.
- **Lock attribute** / **Unlock attribute** (`@atrlock`); a padlock shows while locked.
- **Change owner...**, **Rename...** (the value is copied to the new name and checked before the old attribute is cleared) and **Delete attribute...** (asks first).
- **Copy name**, **Copy as command** (an `&ATTR #12=value` line you can paste) and **Open in the editor**.

Everything in the menu is checked by reading the attribute again, and it is read-only when you do not control the object.

## Moving around

| Key                       | Action                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cmd-P, Ctrl-P             | go to an attribute of the current object by typing part of its name                                        |
| Cmd-1 to Cmd-9            | switch to the first to ninth object tab                                                                    |
| Cmd-T, Ctrl-T             | open another object (the **+** prompt)                                                                     |
| Cmd-W, Ctrl-W             | close the current object tab                                                                               |
| Cmd-click, F12            | go to the attribute named by `u(#12/ATTR)`, `get(...)`, `xget(...)`, `v(...)` and similar under the cursor |
| Cmd-Shift-F, Ctrl-Shift-F | search the values of every attribute of the object                                                         |
| Cmd-Shift-D, Ctrl-Shift-D | show the Object details view                                                                               |
| Cmd-Shift-M, Ctrl-Shift-M | Move the object (when Object details is showing)                                                           |
| Shift-F10, Menu key, F    | the attribute menu for the attribute in the list                                                           |
| Escape                    | back to the terminal (when nothing is selected and no dialog is open)                                      |

Go to definition opens the object in a new tab when it is not open yet. References built at run time, such as `u(%0/ATTR)`, cannot be followed.

Searching all attributes reads every attribute of the object once, so a big object takes a moment; results appear as they come in and the values are kept for the next search. **Refresh** reads the object again.

See also [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys#the-object-editor) and [Commands](help:commands).

topics.title: Keyboard shortcuts
topics.body:
On macOS, **Alt** means the Option key and **Cmd** the Command key. On other systems use Ctrl where Cmd is shown.

## Editing the input line

These are the default bindings of the input line. They follow Emacs and TinyFugue.

| Key                          | Action                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter                        | send the line                                           |
| Shift-Enter                  | insert a new line                                       |
| Tab                          | insert a tab character                                  |
| Escape                       | clear the input line                                    |
| Cmd-Z, Ctrl-Z                | undo typing                                             |
| Cmd-Shift-Z, Ctrl-Y          | redo                                                    |
| Ctrl-A, Home                 | start of line                                           |
| Ctrl-E, End                  | end of line                                             |
| Ctrl-B, Left                 | back one character                                      |
| Ctrl-F, Right                | forward one character                                   |
| Alt-B, Ctrl-Left, Alt-Left   | back one word                                           |
| Alt-F, Ctrl-Right, Alt-Right | forward one word                                        |
| Backspace, Ctrl-H            | delete the character before the cursor                  |
| Delete, Ctrl-D               | delete the character under the cursor                   |
| Ctrl-W, Alt-Backspace        | delete the word before the cursor                       |
| Alt-D                        | delete the word after the cursor                        |
| Ctrl-K                       | delete to the end of the line                           |
| Ctrl-U                       | delete the whole line                                   |
| Ctrl-Y                       | paste the last deleted text                             |
| Ctrl-T                       | swap the two characters around the cursor               |
| Up, Ctrl-P                   | previous history line (prefix search on what you typed) |
| Down, Ctrl-N                 | next history line                                       |

Up, Down, Ctrl-P, Ctrl-N and Shift-Enter are disabled while a password is being typed.

## Multi-line mode

Toggle with Cmd-Shift-E or Ctrl-Shift-E (or the Multi-line button). The editor is a code editor: the Emacs keys above are not used; it has the usual code-editor keys instead.

| Key                               | Action                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cmd-Shift-E, Ctrl-Shift-E         | switch multi-line mode on or off                                   |
| Enter                             | insert a new line                                                  |
| Cmd-Enter, Ctrl-Enter             | send the whole buffer                                              |
| Cmd-Shift-Enter, Ctrl-Shift-Enter | send the selection or the current line                             |
| Tab                               | insert two spaces (indent the selected lines)                      |
| Shift-Tab                         | outdent                                                            |
| Cmd-Alt-], Ctrl-Alt-]             | expand the selection (or everything) over indented lines           |
| Cmd-Alt-[, Ctrl-Alt-[             | collapse it again                                                  |
| Cmd-F, Ctrl-F                     | search (and replace) inside the editor; Escape closes it           |
| Cmd-Z, Ctrl-Z                     | undo                                                               |
| Cmd-Shift-Z, Ctrl-Y               | redo                                                               |
| Escape                            | back to the single line (the text is kept), when no search is open |

## The Object Editor

Open it with `/edit`, the Object Editor button in the top bar, or Cmd-E (Ctrl-E from anywhere except the input line). See [Editing objects and attributes](help:editing).

| Key                       | Action                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cmd-E, Ctrl-E             | switch between the terminal and the editor              |
| Cmd-S, Ctrl-S             | save the current attribute                              |
| Cmd-Shift-S, Ctrl-Shift-S | save every changed attribute of the object              |
| Cmd-P, Ctrl-P             | go to an attribute by name                              |
| Cmd-T, Ctrl-T             | open another object                                     |
| Cmd-W, Ctrl-W             | close the current object tab                            |
| Cmd-1 to Cmd-9            | switch object tab                                       |
| Alt-1 to Alt-9            | switch world                                            |
| Cmd-click, F12            | go to the attribute a call like `u(#12/ATTR)` refers to |
| Cmd-Shift-F, Ctrl-Shift-F | search all attributes of the object                     |
| Cmd-Shift-D, Ctrl-Shift-D | show Object details                                     |
| Cmd-Shift-M, Ctrl-Shift-M | Move the object (in Object details)                     |
| Shift-F10, Menu key, F    | attribute menu for the attribute in the list            |
| Cmd-Alt-], Cmd-Alt-[      | expand, collapse                                        |
| Escape                    | back to the terminal (nothing selected, no dialog open) |

## Resizing the command window

Focus the bar above the input (Tab to it), then:

| Key              | Action                      |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| Up, Down         | one line taller, shorter    |
| PageUp, PageDown | five lines taller, shorter  |
| Home, End        | tallest, smallest           |
| double-click     | reset to the default height |

## History browser

| Key                 | Action                                                         |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ctrl-R, Cmd-Shift-H | open the history browser                                       |
| Up, Down            | select the previous, next entry                                |
| PageUp, PageDown    | move eight entries                                             |
| Ctrl-Home, Ctrl-End | newest, oldest entry                                           |
| Enter               | load the entry into the input (editor if it has several lines) |
| Shift-Enter         | send the entry now                                             |
| Cmd-C, Ctrl-C       | copy the entry (when no text is selected)                      |
| Delete              | remove the entry                                               |
| Escape              | close                                                          |

## Windows and sessions

| Key                       | Action                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Alt-1 to Alt-9            | switch to session 1 to 9                                                  |
| Ctrl-Tab, Ctrl-Shift-Tab  | next and previous session                                                 |
| Cmd-N, Ctrl-Shift-N       | quick connect (macOS menu: Session, New Connection; Windows, Linux: File) |
| Ctrl-O, Cmd-O             | world manager                                                             |
| Ctrl-, and Cmd-,          | the application's settings (macOS: SquatClient menu, Settings...)         |
| Cmd-W, Ctrl-Shift-W       | close the session                                                         |
| Cmd-I, Alt-Enter          | settings of this connection (macOS menu: Session; Windows, Linux: File)   |
| Cmd-Shift-D, Ctrl-Shift-D | suspend: detach from squatters (menu: Session, Suspend)                   |
| Cmd-Shift-R, Ctrl-Shift-R | resume: attach to squatters again (menu: Session, Resume)                 |

## Output and search

| Key                  | Action                                                   |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| PageUp, PageDown     | scroll the output (pauses live output)                   |
| End (output focused) | jump to live output                                      |
| Cmd-F, Ctrl-Shift-F  | search the scrollback (Ctrl-F when the output has focus) |

## Help

| Key                 | Action                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| F1, Cmd-?           | open help                             |
| `/`                 | focus the help search box             |
| Up, Down            | move in the topic tree                |
| Right, Left         | expand, collapse in the tree          |
| Enter               | open the selected topic               |
| Alt-Left, Alt-Right | back, forward in help history         |
| Escape              | clear the search box, then close help |

You can bind keys from scripts with `/bind`; see [Macros: /def](help:scripting/macros-def).

## What next

If a key does not do what you expect, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#ctrl-b-and-ctrl-f-do-not-scroll). To learn what the input line can do, read [Using the client](help:using).

topics.title: Settings reference
topics.body:
Open settings with Ctrl-, (Cmd-, on macOS), the menu (Session, Settings) or the gear button. Changes apply immediately.

| Setting                                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Default                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Theme                                          | Dark, Light, High contrast, or an imported theme                                                                                                                                                                                           | Dark                                                |
| Import theme (JSON)                            | add your own theme from JSON text                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none                                                |
| Font family                                    | font stack for the output and input                                                                                                                                                                                                        | JetBrains Mono, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace |
| Font size (px)                                 | size of text in the output                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 14                                                  |
| Scrollback lines in memory                     | how many lines per tab are kept in memory; older history is fetched on demand                                                                                                                                                              | 20000                                               |
| Minimum contrast                               | 0 turns it off; 4.5 meets WCAG AA; colours are adjusted to reach it                                                                                                                                                                        | 0                                                   |
| Default encoding                               | UTF-8 or Latin-1 for new connections; a world can override it                                                                                                                                                                              | UTF-8                                               |
| Show timestamps                                | prefix each line with its time                                                                                                                                                                                                             | off                                                 |
| Bold text uses bright colours                  | bold basic colours become bright colours                                                                                                                                                                                                   | off                                                 |
| Make bare URLs clickable                       | turn `http://` and `https://` text into links                                                                                                                                                                                              | on                                                  |
| Pause output when scrolled up                  | freeze live output while you read older text                                                                                                                                                                                               | on                                                  |
| Desktop notifications                          | notify about activity in background tabs                                                                                                                                                                                                   | on                                                  |
| Screen-reader mode                             | announce new lines to assistive technology                                                                                                                                                                                                 | off                                                 |
| Command history size                           | entries kept per world, 100 to 1,000,000 (values outside are clamped; 0 is not allowed). Stored on disk for each world and shared by all its sessions; older entries are dropped first. Lowering it trims on the next write and at startup | 20000                                               |
| History of the current world                   | shows how many entries the foreground world has stored, with a **Clear history** button (asks to confirm)                                                                                                                                  | -                                                   |
| Delay between block lines                      | multi-line mode: milliseconds between the lines of a sent block (0 sends them at once); 0 to 10000                                                                                                                                         | 0                                                   |
| Reconnect to squatters automatically           | bring a lost link to a squatter back by itself after sleep or a network drop; your games stay connected on the squatter meanwhile                                                                                                          | on                                                  |
| Editor: join indented lines                    | a line starting with whitespace continues the previous line (leading whitespace removed, nothing inserted)                                                                                                                                 | on                                                  |
| Editor: drop blank and @@ comment lines        | blank lines and lines holding only an `@@` comment are not sent                                                                                                                                                                            | on                                                  |
| Editor: ask before sending unbalanced brackets | before sending from the editor, and in the [upload](help:using#uploading-a-file) dialog, check `( ) [ ] { }` and ask (_Fix first_ or _Send anyway_) when they do not balance                                                               | on                                                  |

The heights of the command window and the editor are set by dragging (see [Using the client](help:using#resizing-the-command-window)); they are saved as settings too.

The scrollback size is applied when the app starts. Truecolour is always on.

Other places that hold settings: worlds ([Connecting and worlds](help:connecting)), squatters ([Squatter](help:squatter)) and scripts ([the scripting language](help:scripting)).

## What next

See [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys) or [Using the client](help:using). If a setting does not seem to work, see [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting).

topics.title: Commands
topics.body:
Anything you type that starts with `/` is a command. Everything else is sent to the game.

## Handled by the app

| Command     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/help`     | open this help; `/help topic` opens a topic and `/help words` searches                                                                                                                                                        |
| `/upload`   | choose a text file and send it line by line; `/upload ~/file.mush` names the file yourself; see [Uploading a file](help:using#uploading-a-file)                                                                               |
| `/edit`     | open the Object Editor; `/edit #12` or `/edit #12/ATTRIBUTE` opens that object or attribute, and `/edit me`, `/edit here` or a name works too; see [Editing objects and attributes](help:editing)                             |
| `/gametype` | show or set what kind of game this is (`/gametype cobramush`, `/gametype other`, `/gametype auto`); it decides whether the Object Editor is offered; see [Editing objects and attributes](help:editing#which-games-it-is-for) |

`/help` is handled by the window itself, so it works even when no world is connected. The browser accepts TinyFugue-style names: `/help def`, `/help /def`, `/help expressions`, `/help triggers`.

## Handled by SquatClient

| Command               | Meaning                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/lua code`           | run a line of Lua; see [Lua scripting](help:lua)                                                                                                                     |
| `/load file`          | load a `.tf` script, or a `.lua` plugin when the name ends in `.lua`                                                                                                 |
| `/reload`             | reload Lua plugins and the startup file                                                                                                                              |
| `/suspend`, `/detach` | let go of squatter sessions and minimise the window; see [Squatter](help:squatter)                                                                                   |
| `/secret text`        | send text without recording it anywhere (never echoed, stored or logged by a squatter); see [Passwords](help:using#passwords)                                        |
| `/colortest`          | print every colour mode (16 colours, the full xterm-256 grid, truecolor gradients, text styles, UTF-8) to compare with a terminal; see [Colours](help:using#colours) |

## TinyFugue-style commands

The scripting language provides the rest. Open any of them with `/help name`.

| Area                | Commands                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Output              | `/echo` `/send` `/beep` `/notify` `/gag` `/hilite`                                                                          |
| Variables           | `/set` `/setenv` `/export` `/unset` `/let` `/listvar` `/shift`                                                              |
| Evaluation          | `/eval` `/test` `/return` `/break` `/builtin`                                                                               |
| Control flow        | `/if` `/elseif` `/else` `/endif` `/while` `/do` `/done` `/for`                                                              |
| Macros and triggers | `/def` `/undef` `/undefn` `/list` `/purge` `/enable` `/disable` `/trigger` `/trigpc` `/hook`                                |
| Keys                | `/bind` `/unbind` `/dokey`                                                                                                  |
| Files               | `/load` `/save` `/require` `/quote`                                                                                         |
| Timers              | `/repeat` `/ps` `/kill`                                                                                                     |
| Worlds              | `/addworld` `/connect` `/dc` `/fg` `/world` `/unworld` `/listworlds` `/listsockets` `/saveworld`                            |
