topics.title: The scripting language
topics.body:
> **SquatClient's scripting language is an original implementation, inspired by and designed to be closely compatible with TinyFugue ("tf").** TinyFugue was written by **Ken Keys** (<https://tinyfugue.sourceforge.net>). Thank you, Ken, and thank you to the TinyFugue community for decades of documentation, scripts and answers. See [About and credits](help:about#tinyfugue).

Most TinyFugue scripts run here as written. SquatClient contains no TinyFugue code, so a few things behave differently, and a few things that only make sense in a terminal are not available. Everything that differs is listed in [TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat).

## The language in one page

Lines that start with `/` are commands; everything else is text for the game. A script is a plain text file (usually ending in `.tf`) of commands that you load with `/load`.

```
/set greeting=Hello
/echo %greeting, world
/def -t'* tells you: *' -ahCgreen tell = /echo Got a tell from %P1
```

- A **macro** is a named list of commands made with `/def`. With `-t` it becomes a **trigger** that runs when matching text arrives from the game. With `-h` it becomes a **hook** that runs on an event such as connecting.
- **Variables** are set with `/set` and read with `%name` or `%{name}`.
- **Expressions** go inside `$[...]` and `/if (...)`.

## Where scripts live

Put commands in a file named `startup.tf` in the SquatClient configuration folder and it is loaded at start (use `/reload` to load it again). Other files can be loaded with `/load filename`. The folder is `SquatClient` inside your system's per-user configuration folder, for example `~/Library/Application Support/SquatClient` on macOS.

## The reference

The pages below this one are the reference for the language, one chapter each. Use `/help name` to jump straight to a command or function, for example `/help def`, `/help strlen` or `/help expressions`. Every example has an **Insert into input** button so you can try it.

## What next

- [Commands](help:commands) lists everything that starts with `/`.
- [Lua scripting](help:lua) is the other language, for larger plugins.
- [TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat) is for people who already know TinyFugue.

topics.title: Lua scripting
topics.body:
SquatClient includes **Lua 5.1** as a second scripting language next to [the TinyFugue-style language](help:scripting). Use Lua for larger, more structured plugins and the TinyFugue-style language for quick triggers and for scripts you already have. The two can call each other.

Lua runs in a sandbox: it cannot read your files or run programs, and a plugin that runs too long is stopped without freezing the client.

## Try it

Everything is in a table called `squat`. Type Lua straight onto the input line with `/lua`:

```
/lua squat.echo("hello from Lua")
```

## Plugins

Plugins are `.lua` files in the `plugins` folder inside the SquatClient configuration folder (for example `~/Library/Application Support/SquatClient/plugins` on macOS). They load when the app starts. Type `/reload` to reload them after changing one.

A first plugin that answers a greeting:

```lua
squat.trigger{
  match = "* says, \"hello\"",
  fn = function(m) squat.send("say Hello, " .. m[1] .. "!") end,
}
```

## The reference

The pages below this one describe every `squat` function. Use `/help squat.on` or any other name to jump to it.

## What next

- [The scripting language](help:scripting) for quick triggers.
- [Commands](help:commands) for `/lua`, `/load` and `/reload`.

topics.title: TinyFugue Script Compatibility
topics.body:
SquatClient's scripting language is modelled on **TinyFugue** ("tf") and designed so that most existing TinyFugue scripts run as written. This page is the short version: what works the same, what is different and why, and what is not available. The pages below it list every command, function, hook and variable.

SquatClient is a new, independent implementation. It contains no TinyFugue code or help text. It follows TinyFugue's documented behaviour and was compared side by side with a real TinyFugue 5.2. Thank you to Ken Keys and the TinyFugue community; see [About and credits](help:about#tinyfugue).

## Summary

|                           | What it covers                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Works the same**        | the command syntax and nearly all commands, macros and triggers with all their options, substitution, expressions, most functions, the hooks, the editing keys and history |
| **Different, on purpose** | safer expressions, deterministic trigger order, scripts never send text by accident, Go-style regular expressions, more colours                                            |
| **Not available**         | features that only make sense in a terminal, a few rarely used commands and functions, shell access                                                                        |

## What works the same

- The command syntax and most commands: `/def`, `/set`, `/let`, `/if`, `/while`, `/for`, `/eval`, `/test`, `/repeat`, `/quote`, `/load`, `/require` and more.
- Macro options `-t -m -h -p -n -F -g -a -P -b -w -E -c`, and glob, simple and regexp patterns.
- Substitution: `%{name}`, `%1` to `%9`, `%*`, `%L`, `%R`, `%P0` to `%P9`, `$[expr]`, `$(command)`.
- The expression language, its operators and most functions, and the hook names.
- The Emacs-style editing keys and the input history.

## What is different, and why

- Inside expressions, `%x` and `%1` are **variable references** and are never read again as text. That stops text from a game from sneaking commands into your scripts.
- `=~` and `!~` compare strings exactly; `=/` and `!/` are glob matches. There is no `%` operator: use `mod()`.
- Triggers fire in a **predictable order**: by priority, then by definition order, and only one macro per priority unless you give `-F`. TinyFugue picks at random among equals.
- Every wildcard of a glob trigger is available as `%P1`, `%P2` and so on.
- A script file that contains a line that is not a command is an **error**. Scripts never send text to a game by accident.
- Backquote command substitution is not provided, because it meant running a shell.
- Colour attributes also accept 256-colour numbers, the `rgb` cube, `grayN` and `#rrggbb` truecolour.
- Every script run has a step limit, a time limit and nesting limits, so a runaway macro cannot freeze the client.
- Regular expressions use the RE2 style: fast and safe, but without look-around or back-references.
- Text is handled in whole characters, so `strlen("é")` is 1.

The complete list, with TinyFugue's behaviour next to SquatClient's, is in [Differences from TinyFugue](help:compat/differences-from-tinyfugue).

## What is not available

SquatClient is a graphical client. Features that exist in TinyFugue only because it ran in a terminal are left out: line wrapping variables (`wrap`, `wrapsize` and friends), the terminal `--More--` prompt (SquatClient pauses the output when you scroll up instead), terminal geometry and signals. Scripts that use them still load: the variables and commands are accepted and ignored. Shell commands such as `/sh` are not available.

A few things are not there yet: `/edit`, `/recordline`, `/watchdog`, and the file stream functions (`tfopen` and friends). They print a clear message when used. See [What is not available yet](help:compat/what-is-not-available-yet).

## How to read the tables

Each entry is labelled **Matches** (tried against a real TinyFugue and identical), **Works** (built from the manual), **Partly**, **Not available yet**, **Handled by the app** or **Not applicable**. See [Reading the matrix](help:compat/reading-the-matrix).

## What next

Start with [the scripting language](help:scripting), or look up a single command in the tables below.

topics.title: What's new
topics.body:
Recent additions you can see and use.

## TinyFugue

- **TinyFugue as a squatter.** Pair with a TinyFugue running on a server, see all its connections and choose who types and who runs triggers. See [TinyFugue as a squatter](help:squatter/tinyfugue).

## Command window

- **Resizable command window.** Drag the bar above the input to make it taller, up to about 70% of the window. Double-click the bar to reset it. See [Using the client](help:using#resizing-the-command-window).
- **Multi-line mode.** A larger editor for writing several lines at once. Press the **Multi-line** button or Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-E. See [Using the client](help:using#multi-line-mode).
- **Command history browser.** Press Ctrl-R (or Cmd-Shift-H) to search everything you have sent to a world, with regular expression and case options. See [Using the client](help:using#history-browser).
- **Command history size.** Choose how many entries each world keeps in [Settings](help:settings).

## Privacy

- **Password protection.** Login and password lines are masked on screen and never saved in history. Use `/secret text` to send anything else privately. See [Passwords](help:using#passwords).

## Colours

- **Terminal-matched colours.** The default dark theme uses a classic terminal palette so games that send the 16 basic colours look like they do in other clients. See [Colours](help:using#colours).
- **`/colortest`.** Prints every colour mode so you can compare SquatClient with another program. See [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting#colours-look-different).

## Writing softcode

- **Code editor with MUSH syntax highlighting.** The code editor colours MUSH functions, brackets and comments so softcode is easier to read.

## Help

- This help was rewritten as a self-contained guide, with a [Troubleshooting](help:troubleshooting) page and a [Glossary](help:glossary). The scripting reference has a [TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat) page.

## What next

Back to the [Home](help:home) page.

topics.title: Troubleshooting

headings.text: Ctrl-B and Ctrl-F do not scroll

topics.body:
Find the symptom, try the steps in order.

## Cannot connect

1. Check the **Host** and **Port** in the world. A typing mistake is the usual cause.
2. Try the other setting for **Use TLS**. A game that offers encryption on one port and plain text on another gives an error or silence on the wrong one.
3. If you see a certificate error and you trust the game, tick **Skip certificate verification** for that world. See [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting#encryption-tls).
4. If the world is set to connect through a squatter, check that the squatter is reachable; see [Lost squatter connection](help:troubleshooting#lost-squatter-connection). Setting **Connect via** to **Direct** shows whether the squatter is the problem.
5. If a world that needs a password fails at once, your operating system keychain may be locked. Unlock it and try again.
6. A tab that says **ended** shows why the game closed the connection. Choose **Connect again** to retry.

## Colours look different

SquatClient shows the colours the game sends, but the 16 basic colours (plain `red`, `green`, `yellow` and so on, plus their bright versions) are not fixed shades. Every terminal and every theme chooses its own, so the same game can look different in different programs. Colours from the 256-colour palette and truecolour are exact everywhere.

- Type `/colortest` to print every colour mode: the 16 basic colours, the full 256-colour grid, truecolour gradients, text styles and UTF-8. Compare it with another program to see what differs.
- The default dark theme uses a classic terminal palette, so games that send basic colours look like they do in TinyFugue.
- If one colour is hard to read, set **Minimum contrast** in [Settings](help:settings), choose another theme, or import a theme of your own. See [Themes](help:using#themes).
- If bold text looks too bright or too dull, try the **Bold text uses bright colours** setting.

## Accents and symbols look garbled

The game is probably sending Latin-1. Set the world's **Encoding** to Latin-1; see [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting#text-encoding).

## Lost squatter connection

If a world routed through a squatter stops responding or the tab shows the squatter link as down:

1. Check that `squatterd` is still running on the server and that the port is open. Try `./squatterd status` on the server.
2. If you reach the server through an ssh tunnel, restart the tunnel. See [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing#when-the-port-is-firewalled).
3. If SquatClient refuses the connection because the fingerprint has changed, **do not trust it** until you know why. Compare the new fingerprint with the one printed by `./squatterd pair`. A legitimate change normally happens only if the server's data folder was reset; then pair again.
4. Your game sessions are not lost while the squatter is running; once the link is back, everything you missed is replayed.
5. A session that shows **ended** lost its game connection (not the squatter). Use **Connect again**.

## Password lines

- Lines such as `connect name password`, `create name password` and `@password ...` are recognised automatically. They are shown masked, for example `connect name ********`, and are never saved in history or in a squatter's record.
- When a game asks for a password and turns echo off, the input line becomes a masked field with a lock icon. History is switched off while you type.
- For anything else that must stay private, type `/secret text`. The text is sent to the game but never shown, saved or logged.
- A password you typed on the input line **before** these protections existed may still be in old history. Open the history browser (Ctrl-R) and delete the entry, or choose **Clear history**.

## History

- Up and Down step through what you sent earlier. If you typed some text first, only lines starting with it are offered.
- Ctrl-R opens the history browser with search. See [Using the client](help:using#history-browser).
- History is kept per world, so a world you never connected from this computer starts empty.
- The **Command history size** setting limits how many entries are kept. Older entries are dropped first.
- A line you sent while the game had echo off, and password lines, are deliberately never saved.

## Ctrl-B and Ctrl-F do not scroll

On the input line these are Emacs editing keys, as in TinyFugue: Ctrl-B moves the cursor back one character and Ctrl-F forward one. To scroll the output use PageUp and PageDown. To search the output use Cmd-F (Ctrl-Shift-F elsewhere). All keys are in [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys).

## The output stopped moving

You scrolled up, so SquatClient paused the output to let you read. The status bar shows **--More--** and a count of lines that arrived meanwhile. Press End or use the jump button to go back to live output. You can turn this off with **Pause output when scrolled up** in [Settings](help:settings).

## Still stuck

Search this help (press `/` inside it), or report the problem in the repository linked in [About and credits](help:about#source-code).

topics.title: Glossary
topics.body:
Short explanations of words used in this help and in MU* games.

## Client terms

**World**: a saved connection to a game: its name, host, port and login. See [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting).

**Session**: one live (or ended) connection. Each session has a tab.

**Squatter**: a small program (`squatterd`) on a server that keeps your sessions running while SquatClient is closed. See [Squatter](help:squatter).

**Direct**: a world setting meaning the connection goes straight from your computer to the game and ends when the app closes.

**Pairing**: the one-time step that lets SquatClient talk to a squatter, confirmed with a fingerprint.

**Fingerprint**: a short code that identifies a squatter's encryption certificate. You compare it once while pairing.

**Scrollback**: the lines you can scroll back to.

## Scripting terms

**Macro**: a named list of commands made with `/def`. You run it by typing `/name`.

**Trigger**: a macro that runs automatically when a line from the game matches a pattern. See [Macros: /def](help:scripting/macros-def).

**Hook**: a macro that runs when an event happens, such as connecting or disconnecting.

**Pattern**: the text a trigger looks for. A **glob** pattern uses `*` for any text and `?` for one character. A **regexp** is a regular expression.

**Variable**: a named value you set with `/set` and read with `%name`.

**Attribute** (in scripts): the colour and style of text, such as bold or red. See [Attributes](help:scripting/attributes).

**Plugin**: a Lua file that adds behaviour; see [Lua scripting](help:lua).

## Game terms

**MU\***: MUDs, MUSHes, MUXes, MOOs and similar text games.

**MUSH**: a kind of MU* where players build objects and write programs in the game itself.

**Softcode**: the programs players write inside a MUSH, as opposed to the server's own code (hardcode).

**dbref**: the number that identifies every object in a MUSH, written with a hash sign, such as `#123`.

**Attribute** (in a MUSH): a named piece of text stored on an object, for example a description or a command. Not the same as a text attribute above.

## What next

Back to the [Home](help:home) page.

topics.title: Reference overview
topics.body:
SquatClient's scripting language is modelled on **TinyFugue** ("tf"), the
long-loved MU* client written by **Ken Keys**
(<https://tinyfugue.sourceforge.net>). It is designed so that most existing
TinyFugue scripts run as written: the commands, macros, triggers, hooks and
expressions work the way TinyFugue users expect.

It is a new, independent implementation. It contains no TinyFugue code, so a
few things behave differently, and some things that only make sense in a
terminal are not available. Everything that differs is listed in
[TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat). Thank you, Ken, and thank you
to the TinyFugue community for decades of documentation, scripts and answers.

In this reference "TF" means TinyFugue.

Scripts are plain text files (`.tf`). Everything below can be typed on the
input line, put in a script and loaded with `/load`, or run by triggers and hooks.

topics.title: Input lines, statements and scripts
topics.body:
* A line that starts with `/` is a **command**. Any other line is **text** and is
  sent to the world (not expanded, unless `/set sub=on`).
* A command line is split into **statements** at `%;` only (a plain `;` is
  ordinary text, as in TinyFugue: `/echo a;b` prints `a;b`). Separators inside
  `$[...]`, `$(...)` and `%{...}` do not split. `/def`, `/repeat` and `/eval`
  take the rest of the line, keeping `%;` unsplit so that it separates
  statements when their body runs later:

  ```
  /def greet = /echo hello %; /echo again     ; the whole body is stored
  ```

  Trailing blanks before a `%;` are dropped.
* **Script files**: blank lines and lines starting with `;` are ignored; a line
  ending in `\` continues on the next line (leading blanks of the next line are
  dropped). Every other line must be a command (non-command lines in a file are
  an error: a script never sends text by accident). Blocks (`/if`, `/while`,
  `/do`, `/for`) may span lines and are collected until their `/endif` /
  `/done`.
* Errors print as `% message` and the script keeps going,
  except that an error inside a loop body ends the loop. At most 20 errors are
  shown per run.

topics.title: Substitution
topics.body:
Performed on the arguments of ordinary commands and on every statement of a
macro body when it runs.

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `%%` | a literal `%` |
| `%;` | a literal `;` (when it survives splitting) |
| `%name`, `%{name}` | variable (local first, then global); unset is empty |
| `%1`..`%9`, `%{N}` | positional parameters (words of the arguments) |
| `%*` | all arguments as typed; `%#` their count; `%0` the macro name |
| `%PL` `%PR` | text left / right of the last regexp match; `%L` is the last positional parameter, `%R` a random one |
| `%-N` `%{-N}` `%-L` | all parameters but the first N / but the last |
| `%{sel-default}` | the default when the selector expands to nothing |
| `%P0`..`%P9`, `%{P12}` | match parts: `P0` the whole match, `P1`.. captures |
| `%?` | return value of the last command or macro |
| `%{?name}` | `1` if the variable is set, else `0` (extension) |
| `${name}` | the body of macro `name` (an error if there is none) |
| `\c` `\n` | the character `c` with no special meaning (`\%`, `\$`, `\\`); `\65` / `\0x41` / `\0101` the character with that decimal / hex / octal code |
| `$[expr]` | value of an expression |
| `$(command)` | what the command echoed (lines joined by spaces); if it echoed nothing, its `/return` value |
| `$$` | a literal `$` |

Substitution is a single pass: substituted text is not rescanned, so text from
the MUD can never inject commands through `%*`. `/eval` expands its arguments
and then runs the result, which expands again:

```
/set cmd=/echo hi
/eval %cmd              ; runs /echo hi
/eval /echo %%{x}       ; first pass leaves %{x}, second pass expands it
```

**Triggers** receive `%*` = the line, `%1..` = its words, `%P0` = the whole match,
`%P1..` = glob wildcards or regexp groups in order, `%PL`/`%PR` for regexp
triggers.

topics.title: Expressions
topics.body:
Used by `$[...]`, `/test`, `/if`, `/elseif`, `/while`, `/do..while`, `/for`,
`/return`, `/def -E` and `test()`/`eval()`.

Values are integers (int64), floats, or strings. Text that looks like a number
is a number. In arithmetic, text counts by its leading number: `"12abc" * 2` is
24 and plain words are 0. Truth: the numeric value is non-zero, so plain words
and the empty string are false (as in TF). A float prints with 15 significant
digits and, when it is a whole non-negative number, a trailing dot: `pow(2,10)`
is `1024.`, `0.1+0.2` is `0.3` (TF output, verified). The on/off ("enumerated")
variables such as `gag` read as 1/0 in an expression and `on`/`off` as text.

Operators, lowest to highest precedence:

| | |
|---|---|
| `,` | sequence (value of the last) |
| `:=` `+=` `-=` `*=` `/=` | assignment to a variable (right associative) |
| `a ? b : c` | conditional |
| `\|` `\|\|` | logical or (short-circuit; the value is the last operand evaluated; `\|\|` is an extension) |
| `&` `&&` | logical and (short-circuit; value of the last operand evaluated; `&&` is an extension) |
| `=` `==` `!=` `<` `>` `<=` `>=` `=~` `!~` `=/` `!/` | one precedence level, left to right. `=`/`==`/`!=`/`<`.. compare numerically (leading-number coercion); when neither side starts with a number they compare as text (TF would call any two words equal). `=~` `!~` exact string equal / not equal (never numeric). `=/` `!/` glob match / no match (case-insensitive): `str =/ "pat*"` |
| `+` `-` | add, subtract |
| `*` `/` | multiply, divide (integer division when both are integers; division by zero is an error) |
| `!` `-` `+` `++x` `--x` | unary, prefix increment |
| `x++` `x--` | postfix |

Barewords are variables (`x`); `name(args)` calls a function; `{x}`, `{1}`, `{*}`,
`{#}` and `%x`, `%1`, `%*`, `%#`, `%{name}` read variables and parameters
**without** re-parsing the value as expression text (prefer these for script
input). There is no `%` operator (use `mod()`); `%` is not interpolated inside
string literals (use `strcat`). A `$[expr]` inside an expression is evaluated
first (so `/return $[1+2]` works). String literals use `"` or `'` with `\n \t \r \e
\\ \"` escapes. Numbers: `12`, `1.5`, `.5`, `1e3`, `0x1f` (hex, `x++` and `x--` are extensions).

A user macro can be called like a function: `/def add = /return {1} + {2}` then
`$[add(2, 3)]`.

topics.title: Variables
topics.body:
* `/set name=value` (or `/set name value`) always sets a **global** (a local of
  the same name still shadows it while the macro runs). `name := value` in an
  expression assigns the nearest variable, else a global.
* `/let name=value` creates/sets a **local** that lives until the macro returns.
  Locals are dynamically scoped: macros called from it can see them. A `/for`
  counter does not outlive its loop.
* `/setenv name=value` is `/set` plus marking it exported; `/export name` marks an
  existing one. `/unset name`. `/listvar [glob]`. `/set` alone lists everything.
* Names are `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. Values are strings that act as numbers
  when numeric.
* TF's on/off variables (`gag hilite more wrap visual borg login ...`) store
  `on` or `off` whatever you assign (`1`, `0`, `on`, `off`). Their defaults are
  TinyFugue's own (checked against a real TinyFugue; see [Variables](help:compat/variables)).
* Behavioural variables read by the interpreter: `gag` and `hilite` (`off`
  disables gag/hilite effects), `matching` (default `/def` match mode),
  `hiliteattr` (attribute used by `/hilite`, default `B`), `sub` (`on` expands
  `%` in typed text), `quiet`, `ptime` (default `/repeat` delay), `wordpunct`,
  `TZ` (`UTC` or a fixed offset such as `UTC+2`, `-0530`, used by
  `ftime`/`mktime`), `visual` (a layout switch handled by the app),
  `histsize`. Others from TinyFugue are accepted as ordinary variables.

topics.title: Macros: /def
topics.body:
```
/def [options] [name] [= body]
```

The body is stored unexpanded and expanded each time the macro runs. Calling
`/name args` runs it with `%1..` set from `args`. A macro may also be a
trigger, a hook, or a key binding. Options (no space between the letter and its
value; quote values containing spaces with `'..'`, `".."` or `{..}`):

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-t<pattern>` | trigger on received text matching the pattern |
| `-m<glob\|simple\|regexp>` | pattern style (default `glob`, or `$matching`) |
| `-h<HOOK [argpattern]>` | run when the hook fires (optional glob over the hook's arguments) |
| `-p<n>` | priority (default 1; higher runs first) |
| `-n<shots>` / `-1` | delete the macro after that many firings |
| `-F` | fall-through: after firing, let lower-priority matches fire too |
| `-a<attrs>` | highlight the whole line (see [Attributes](help:scripting/attributes)); `g` in the attrs gags (`-g` alone is an extension) |
| `-P<n><attrs>` | highlight part `n` (0 whole match, 1..9 capture/wildcard) |
| `-b<key>` | bind to a key name (see `/bind`) |
| `-w<world>` | only active for that world |
| `-E<expr>` | extra condition; must be true for the macro to fire |
| `-c<percent>` | fire with that probability (`-c0` never; a macro that loses the roll is simply not a match) |
| `-i` | invisible: not listed by `/list`, and `/purge` skips it unless given `-i` |

Single-letter options may be clustered (`-Fp2`, `-ag`).

Patterns:

* **glob** matches the *whole* line, ignoring case: `*` any text, `?` one
  character, `[a-z]` / `[^a-z]` classes, `{red|blue}` whole-word alternatives
  (they must start at the beginning or after a space and end before a space or
  the end; alternatives may contain wildcards), `\*` a literal. Write
  `*dragon*` to match anywhere. Each wildcard becomes `%P1..`.
* **simple**: the line must equal the pattern exactly (case-sensitive).
* **substr**: the line must contain the pattern.
* **regexp**: Go (RE2) syntax, matches anywhere in the line, `%P0..`, `%PL`,
  `%PR`. As in TF a pattern with no upper-case letter matches case-insensitively.
  The positional parameters of any trigger are the words of the line.

Dispatch: matching macros are ordered by priority (high first), then definition
order. The first one fires; if it has `-F` the next fires too, and so on. Only
one macro per priority level fires unless `-F` is used (a deliberate
simplification: TF picks randomly among equals; otherwise identical). A hook fires its macros the
same way; hook arguments become `%1..`.

Other macro commands:

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `/undef name...` | remove macros by name |
| `/undefn N...` | remove by number shown in `/list` |
| `/list [glob]` | list definitions in TF's format (`% N: /def -p1 -mglob -t'..' name = body`) |
| `/purge [-i] [glob]` | remove all (or matching) visible macros; `-i` includes invisible ones |
| `/enable name...` `/disable name...` | extension: switch a macro off/on without deleting it |
| `/gag [pat [= body]]` / `/hilite [pat [= body]]` / `/partial regexp` | define a gag / `-a$hiliteattr` / partial-hilite trigger; with no argument `/gag` and `/hilite` turn the effect on; `/nogag` `/nohilite` remove or turn off |
| `/trig pat = body`, `/trigp pri pat = body`, `/trigc pct pat = body`, `/trigpc pri pct pat = body` | define unnamed trigger macros |
| `/hook EVENT[ pat] = body` | define a hook macro (`/def -h`); `/unhook EVENT [pat]`, `/untrig [-a..] pat`, `/undeft pat` remove by exact pattern |
| `/trigger [-gnl] [-w[world]] [-hEVENT] text` | run trigger (or hook) macros as if `text` had arrived; `-n` / `-l` list what would match instead |
| `/bind key = command`, `/unbind key` | key bindings |
| `/dokey name` | editing actions (`LEFT RIGHT HOME END WLEFT WRIGHT BSPC DCH BWORD DWORD DEOL DLINE`) work on the input line and return the cursor; other actions are passed to the app |
| `/save file [glob]`, `/load [-q] file`, `/require file` | files (gated by `/restrict`) |

Redefining a name replaces the macro and fires the `REDEF` hook. A macro name
shadows a built-in command of the same name; `/builtin name args` runs the
built-in.

topics.title: Attributes
topics.body:
An attribute string is a comma-separated list; each item is flag letters
optionally followed by one colour clause:

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | normal: reset styling first |
| `h` or `B` | bold |  
| `d` `i` `u` `s` `f` `r` | dim, italic, underline, strike, flash/blink, reverse |
| `g` | gag |
| `C<colour>` | foreground colour |
| `BC<colour>` | background colour |

Colours: `black red green yellow blue magenta cyan white` (0-7), `bright` + name
(8-15), a palette index `0`..`255` (xterm-256), `rgbRGB` (6x6x6 cube, digits
0-5, e.g. `rgb530`), `gray0`..`gray23`, and 24-bit `#rrggbb` or `#rgb`.

```
/echo -aCred,u red underlined
/echo -aC196 palette 196
/echo -aC#ff8800,BC#001122 truecolour on truecolour
/def -t'*dragon*' -ahC#ff4040 dragon
/def -mregexp -t'(\d+) gold' -P1BCyellow,C0 gold
```

**Inline markup** (`/echo -p`, `echo()`, `encode_attr`): `@{attrs}` changes the
current attributes (they accumulate; `@{n}` resets), `@@` is a literal `@`:
`/echo -p @{Cred}red@{n} plain @{C#00ff00}green`.

topics.title: Control flow
topics.body:
```
/if (expr) commands
/elseif (expr) commands
/else commands
/endif

/while (expr)        ; /do directly after the header is optional
  ...
/done

/do
  ...
/while (expr)

/for var first last command        ; TF form: one statement
/for var first last commands /done ; block form
/break      /return [expr]
```

Commands after a header on the same line are the first statements of that body;
separate statements with `%;` inside macro bodies:

```
/def count = /let i=1 %; /while (i <= {1}) %; /echo %i %; /let i=$[i+1] %; /done
```

(`/let` and `/set` store text: `/let i=i+1` would store the string `i+1`; use
`$[...]` to compute.)

In the TF form of `/for` the whole line is substituted once before the loop
(exactly as in TinyFugue), so a body that wants the counter writes `%%i`
(second pass) rather than `%i`; the counter is a local that vanishes after the
loop. The block form (`/done`) substitutes per iteration. `/do ... /while (expr)`
is an extension; TF's `/while list /do list /done` and `/if list /then` forms
(a command list as the condition) are not available.
A typed line closes unfinished blocks at its end; in a script file an
unfinished block is an error. Every run is limited; see [Limits and safety](help:scripting/limits-and-safety).

topics.title: Commands
topics.body:
`/help` lists them and `/help name` prints usage.

* Output: `/echo [-w world] [-a attrs] [-p] text`, `/send [-w world] text`,
  `/beep`, `/notify title | body` (extension), `/gag`, `/hilite`.
* Variables/eval: `/set /setenv /export /unset /let /listvar /shift [n]
  /eval /test /return /break /builtin`.
* Macros/files: see [Macros: /def](help:scripting/macros-def).
* Processes: `/repeat [-w[world]] [-n] [-<time>|-S] <count|i> <command>` runs a
  command repeatedly (time is seconds,
  `h:m` or `h:m:s`; without a time `$ptime` (1 s) is used; `-S` runs it now,
  synchronously; `-n` runs the first one immediately); it returns the process
  id. `/ps [-sr] [pid]` lists processes in TF's table format, `/kill pid...`
  stops them.
* `/quote [-dsend|echo|exec] [prefix] 'file` runs each line of a file (needs file
  access) and `/quote [prefix] #command` each line a command echoes; every line
  becomes `prefix + line`. Shell forms (`!cmd`, `` `cmd` ``) are not available.
* Worlds (need world access): `/addworld [-Ttype] [-x] name [char pass] host port`,
  `/connect [world]`, `/dc [world]`, `/fg [world]`, `/world name`, `/unworld`,
  `/listworlds [glob]`, `/listsockets`, `/saveworld`.
* Display commands (handled by the app): `/limit /unlimit /relimit
  /recall /log /localecho /status_add /status_edit /status_rm /histsize`.
  `/input text` inserts at the cursor of the input line; `/suspend` and the
  `visual` variable are passed to the app.
* `/version /features /help /restrict [shell|file|world] /exit /quit`.

`/restrict` raises (never lowers) the restriction level: `shell` (always in
force; there is no shell access), `file` (no `/load /save /quote 'file /log`),
`world` (also no world/connection commands). SquatClient sets the initial
level.

topics.title: Functions
topics.body:
Strings: `strlen strcat strcmp strncmp strchr strrchr strstr strrep substr pad
tolower toupper replace substitute ascii char strcmpattr textencode textdecode`
(indices are in characters, 0 based and clamped; a negative index counts from
the end (`substr(s, -2)` is the last two characters); `strchr(s, set [, start])`
is the first position of any character of `set`, or -1; `tolower(s [, n])` only
changes the first n characters;
`pad(s, w)` right-justifies in `w` columns, a negative width left-justifies;
`replace(old, new, s)` replaces every occurrence of old in s (TF argument order); `substitute(text [, attrs [,
inline]])` replaces the line being processed by a trigger).

Regexp: `regmatch(pattern, string)` returns the number of captured substrings
including `%P0` (0 when there is no match) and sets `%P0..%P9`, `%PL`, `%PR`
for the rest of the macro. A pattern without upper-case letters is
case-insensitive.

Math: `abs sin cos tan asin acos atan exp ln log10 pow sqrt rand trunc mod`
(`rand(n)` is 0..n-1; `rand(a, b)` is inclusive; `trunc` and `mod` return integers;
`pow`, `sqrt` and the rest return floats).

Time: `time()` (Unix seconds), `mktime(y [,m [,d [,h [,mi [,s [,us]]]]]])`, `ftime(format [, secs])`
(strftime codes `%Y %y %m %d %e %H %I %M %S %p %a %A %b %B %j %Z %z %s %F %T %R
%D %c %n %t %%`), `idle([world])` seconds since last input, `sidle([world])`
since last send.

Misc: `eval(str)` (expand and run as commands, returns the echoed text), `test(expr)`,
`whatis(v)` (`int`, `float`, `string`), `getopts(optstring [, args])` (sets locals
`opt_x`, returns the remaining arguments), `echo(str [, attrs [, inline [, world]]])`,
`send(str [, world])`, `prompt(str)`, `world_info([world,] field)` (`name host port
character type tls connected`), `is_connected([world])`, `is_open`, `fg_world()`,
`nactive()`, `columns()`, `lines()`, `winlines()`, `isatty()` (1), `systype()`,
`nlog() nmail() nread() morepaused() moresize() morescroll() getpid()
gethostname() cputime() filename()` (neutral values: no mail, no paging).

Input line (the app's input line; positions are
characters): `kbhead() kbtail() kbpoint() kblen() kbgoto(i) kbdel(i)
kbmatch([i]) kbwordleft([i]) kbwordright([i]) kbcharback([n]) kbcharfwd([n])`.
Built-in commands can also be called as functions with one argument, e.g.
`repeat("-60 1 /echo hi")`.

Attributes: `encode_attr(text, attrs)`, `decode_attr(text)` (markup to an ANSI
string with 16/256/24-bit codes), `strip_attr(text)` (remove markup and ANSI).

topics.title: Hooks
topics.body:
`/def -hNAME [argpattern] name = body`. Names: `ACTIVITY ATCP BAMF BGTEXT BGTRIG
CONFAIL CONFLICT CONNECT DISCONNECT GMCP ICONFAIL KILL LOAD LOADFAIL LOG LOGIN
MAIL MORE NOMACRO OPTION102 PENDING PREACTIVITY PROCESS PROMPT PROXY REDEF RESIZE
SEND SHADOW SHELL SIGHUP SIGTERM SIGUSR1 SIGUSR2 WORLD`. SquatClient raises
`CONNECT DISCONNECT CONFAIL LOGIN WORLD SEND PROMPT ACTIVITY BGTEXT BGTRIG LOAD
LOADFAIL REDEF RESIZE GMCP` itself. The others can be defined, so scripts that
use them still load, but nothing raises them. `SEND` fires just before text is
sent (a `SEND` hook that sends does not trigger itself), `LOAD` and `LOADFAIL`
fire around `/load`, and `REDEF` fires when a macro is redefined (arguments
`macro NAME`; an identical redefinition is silent). `/trigger -hNAME args` fires a hook by hand;
`/hook NAME[ pat] = body` defines one. Hook arguments are `%1..`, e.g. `GMCP`
gets `%1` = package, `%2` = JSON. Hook names are fixed (an unknown name is an
error).

topics.title: Limits and safety
topics.body:
Every top-level run (an input line, a received line, a hook, a key, a timer, one
logical line of a loaded file) has:

* a step budget (statements, loop iterations, expression evaluations, function
  calls; default 50 000),
* a time limit (default 2 seconds),
* a macro nesting limit (default 64) and file nesting limit (16),
* a 256 KB cap on any one string value.

Exceeding a limit aborts that run with `% script budget exceeded: ...`; the
interpreter stays usable. When a line is replayed (for example the lines you missed while detached from a squatter) no macro body runs, nothing is sent or notified, no shot is
consumed and no variable is changed; only gag and highlight are computed.

topics.title: Examples
topics.body:
```
; keep-alive every five minutes
/def -hCONNECT on_connect = /repeat -300 100000 /send IDLE
; highlight tells and notify
/def -mregexp -t'^(\w+) tells you: (.*)$' -P1Cbrightgreen,h tell = \
    /notify Tell from %P1 | %P2
; gag spam, but only from one world
/def -wmain -t'\[Spam\]*' -g spam
; auto-loot with a condition and a 50% chance
/def -t'* is dead.' -E'looting' -c50 loot = get all from corpse
; 256 and truecolour
/def -t'*ALERT*' -a'BC#400000,C#ffe0e0,h' alert
; a helper with a return value
/def max = /return {1} > {2} ? {1} : {2}
/echo biggest: $[max(3, 9)]
```

topics.title: Reading the matrix
topics.body:
SquatClient's scripting language is modelled on TinyFugue ("tf") and designed
so that most existing TinyFugue scripts run as written. It is a new,
independent implementation: it contains no TinyFugue code or help text, and it
follows TinyFugue's documented behaviour. This reference lists, command by
command, function by function, hook by hook and variable by variable, how each
one compares. For a short overview read
[TinyFugue Script Compatibility](help:compat) first.

The behaviour was also checked side by side against a real TinyFugue 5.2: about
460 test lines in 39 groups. In 29 groups the results are identical; the other
10 differ only in the deliberate ways listed under
[Differences from TinyFugue](help:compat/differences-from-tinyfugue).

Every entry in the tables below has one of these labels:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Matches** | tried against a real TinyFugue and gives the same result (apart from the listed differences) |
| **Works** | implemented from the TinyFugue manual; not compared with a real TinyFugue |
| **Partly** | works, with the limit stated |
| **Not available yet** | not there yet: the command is accepted and ignored, or gives an error, as stated |
| **Handled by the app** | SquatClient decides what it means (the window, the input line and so on) |
| **Not applicable** | makes no sense in a graphical client |

The rule behind all of this: match TinyFugue, unless TinyFugue's behaviour is a
clear trap (for example, text from a game reaching expression source), and
document every deliberate difference.

topics.title: Differences from TinyFugue
topics.body:
| Area | Real TinyFugue | SquatClient |
|---|---|---|
| Expression substitution | `%x` text substitution happens inside expressions | Inside `$[..]`, `/if (..)` etc. `%x`, `%1`, `%*`, `%{x}` are **variable references** (never re-parsed as expression text); `%` is not interpolated in string literals. Removes a code-injection hazard from MUD text. `$[..]` nested inside an expression is supported (as TF). |
| Top-level lines | a typed line or a script-file line is **not** substituted (only macro bodies and `/eval` are): `/echo %x` prints `%x` | lines are substituted like a macro body, so `/echo $[1+2]` typed or in a file prints 3. Scripts that work in TF (they put logic in macros) behave the same. |
| `==` `!=` `<` `>` .. on words | numeric only, so any two non-numeric strings are "equal" (`"abc" == "abd"` is 1) | numeric when either side starts with a number (identical to TF, including `"12abc" == 12`); plain text compared with plain text is compared as **text**. `=~ !~` are the exact string forms in both. |
| Operators `&&` `\|\|` `x++` `x--` `0x1f` | rejected (error) | accepted extensions |
| Integers | 32-bit-ish: results beyond that become reals (`9999999999*3` prints `29999999997.`) | int64 arithmetic, wraps on overflow |
| Float text | `0.1+0.2` prints `0.3`; `1.0*3` is `3.`; a literal keeps its text (`1.0`) | same 15-digit format and trailing dot, except literals print normalised (`$[1.0]` is `1.`) |
| Equal-priority triggers | one chosen at random | deterministic: priority desc, then definition order; the first fires (`-F` continues) |
| Glob captures | `%1..` are the words of the line | `%1..` are the words (as TF) and in addition `%P1..` are the glob wildcards (`%P0` the line) |
| Script files | a non-command line is sent as text | a non-command line in a loaded file is an **error** (no accidental sends); an unclosed block is an error |
| Error handling | an error ends the macro | errors are shown as `% msg` and the macro continues, except that an error inside a loop body ends the loop; at most 20 errors per run |
| `/def` of a built-in name | `CONFLICT` hook message | the macro shadows the built-in; `/builtin cmd` reaches the built-in |
| `/set name = value` | stores `= value` (and warns) | spaces around `=` are accepted |
| `$(command)` | command substitution | returns the echoed lines joined by spaces, else the `/return` value; backquote `` `cmd` `` is **not available** (it implied a shell) |
| After a failed substitution (`${nosuchmacro}`) | the command still runs with an empty result | the command is abandoned |
| `/return` with no value in a function call | the call yields 0 | yields the empty string |
| Strings | byte strings (`strlen("é")` is 2) | UTF-8 characters (`strlen("é")` is 1; `substr`, `tolower` etc. count characters) |
| `strcmp strncmp` | difference of the first differing bytes (platform dependent) | `-1`, `0` or `1` |
| Regexps | PCRE2 | Go RE2: no look-around or back-references. `regmatch()` counts groups like TF and the caseless-if-no-capital rule is implemented. |
| `whatis(x)` | looks at the unevaluated operand (`decimal` for a literal real, `id:string` for a variable) | `int`, `float`, `string` of the value |
| `winlines()`, `fg_world()` | `lines()-1` (status line); empty with no socket | the output pane height; the foreground world name |
| `/list` attribute letters | lists a hilite as `-aB` | lists it as written (`-ah`) |
| `/trigger -h` | also displays the hook's default message | runs the hook macros only |
| `SEND` hook | not invoked by `/send` or `send()` unless enabled | fired just before text is sent (does not recurse) |
| `/repeat -P` | repeat on prompt | not supported |
| `TZ` | system zones | `UTC` and fixed offsets only |
| `/do .. /while (e)` | not a TF construct | accepted extension; TF's `/while list /do list /done` and `/if list /then` forms (a command list as condition) are not available |
| Budgets | none | every run has a step budget, wall deadline, nesting and string-size limits (see [Limits and safety](help:scripting/limits-and-safety)) |
| Colours | 16/8 colours | attribute strings also accept xterm-256 indices (`C196`), `rgbRGB`, `gray0..23`, truecolour `#rrggbb`; letters `i` (italic), `s` (strike) are additions; `-g` alone is a gag shorthand |
| Extensions | | `/notify`, `/enable`, `/disable`, `/builtin`, `/return` as a command, `%{?name}`, `-E`/`-c` on hooks |

Where an early version disagreed with a real TinyFugue it was fixed, so these
now behave as in TinyFugue: `;` is plain text (only
`%;` separates), `=` is equality (assignment is `:=`), `&`/`|` return the last
operand, float formatting, leading-number coercion, text truthiness, `replace()`
argument order `(old, new, str)`, negative `substr`/`strstr`/`strchr` indexes,
`%L`/`%PL`/`%PR`/`%-N`/`%{sel-default}`, backslash escapes, `${macro}`,
case-insensitive globs and whole-word `{a|b}`, `[^..]` only, regexps caseless
without capitals, `-msubstr`, default priority 1, `/for var a b command`,
dynamic scope of `/let` and global-only `/set`, `/purge` skipping invisible
macros, `/hook` defining hooks, `/trigpc` defining a trigger, `/ps` format and
`/repeat` semantics, `regmatch()` count, `ascii("")` is 0, `mktime` arguments.

topics.title: What is not part of a graphical client
topics.body:
Only two families of TinyFugue features are left out on purpose: line
**wrapping** (`wrap wraplog wrapspace wrapsize`) and **paging** (`more morepaused
morescroll moresize`). Their variables exist (with TinyFugue's defaults) and are
accepted and ignored, and the functions return neutral values (`morepaused()` is
0). SquatClient does its own wrapping and has a "pause when scrolled up"
setting instead.

Everything else is supported, with a graphical meaning where needed:

| Feature | In SquatClient |
|---|---|
| Process commands `/ps /kill /repeat` (and `/quote` processes) | **Matches**. `/sh` and `/quote !` do not exist because there is no shell access; `/restrict` can also switch off file and world commands |
| Input-line functions and `/input /dokey /bind` | **Matches**; they work on the app's input line |
| `visual` (split input/status layout), `/dokey redraw`, `/suspend` | handled by the app (`/suspend` detaches squatter sessions; the others do nothing). `/visual` is not a command in TinyFugue either; `visual` is a variable |
| Terminal size: `columns() lines() winlines()`, `isatty()` (always 1), status fields | **Works**: the size is that of the output pane; `status_*` variables are stored; `status_fields()` is **not available yet** |
| `/core` and the terminal signal hooks `SIGHUP SIGTERM SIGUSR1 SIGUSR2` | **Not applicable** (you can define them; they never fire) |
| `/lcd`, `/sh` | **Not applicable** |

topics.title: Commands
topics.body:
| Command | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| addworld connect dc fg world unworld saveworld listworlds listsockets | Works | `-p -e -s` are accepted and ignored; SquatClient stores the worlds |
| localecho | Works | switches echo of what you type |
| def | **Matches** | options `-t -m -h -p -n -1 -F -a -E -c -w -b -i -P -q` |
| undef undefn | **Matches** (undef) / Works (undefn) | `/undef` of an unknown name is an error, as in TinyFugue |
| list | **Partly** | the output format is identical (`/list name`); there are no `-t/-h/-m/-b/-s` filters yet |
| purge | **Partly** | name glob and `-i`; TinyFugue's other `/list`-style options are not available |
| trigger | **Matches** | `-g -n -l -w -h`; `-n` output layout as TinyFugue |
| trig trigp trigc trigpc | **Matches** | define unnamed triggers |
| gag hilite partial nogag nohilite | **Matches** (gag, hilite listing) / Works | `/gag pat = body`; the no-argument forms switch the variables |
| hook unhook untrig undeft | **Matches** (hook, untrig) / Works | `/hook EVENT pat = body` defines; `/trigger -h` fires. Unknown hook names are errors |
| save | Partly | writes macros only (not variables or worlds) |
| load require | Works | `-q` is accepted; there is no search path; fires LOAD and LOADFAIL |
| set let setenv export unset listvar shift | **Matches** | `/set` global, `/let` dynamic locals, on/off variables normalise to on/off |
| eval test return break | **Matches** | |
| if elseif else endif while done | **Matches** | the command-list forms (`/if cmd %; /then`) are not available |
| for | **Matches** | TinyFugue form `/for v a b cmd` and the `/done` block form |
| echo | **Matches** | `-a -p -w -e`; inline `@{attr}` markup; a leading `-N` argument is an option, as in TinyFugue |
| beep | Works | rings the bell |
| recall limit unlimit relimit log bind unbind dokey input status_add status_edit status_rm histsize | Handled by the app / **Matches** (input, dokey editing) | where TinyFugue talks to the terminal, the app takes over; `/log` is switched off by `/restrict file` |
| repeat ps kill | **Matches** | `-S -n -time i`, `$ptime`, TinyFugue's table format |
| quote | Partly | the `'file` and `#cmd` forms; `-dsend/-decho/-dexec`; the shell forms are not available |
| help | Partly | prints a usage line per command; use the help browser for details (`/help`) |
| exit quit | Works | closes the app |
| restrict | Works | shell / file / world |
| version features | Partly | fixed text |

topics.title: What is not available yet
topics.body:
* Command-list conditions (`/if cmd %; /then`, `/while cmd %; /do`), backquote
  substitution, `/edit`, `/recordline`, file streams (the `tfopen` family),
  `/watchdog`, `/watchname`, the grapheme functions, `encode_ansi` and
  `decode_ansi`, `status_fields`, most of the rarely used hooks, `/repeat -P`.
* `/list` and `/purge` filters other than the name glob and `-i`; saving
  variables with `/save`; IANA time zone names.
* A real TinyFugue logs plain text only, so colour and highlight behaviour
  (`-a`, `-P`) was implemented from the manual and is marked **Works**, not
  **Matches**. Anything interactive (the real keyboard, `/more`) and timing
  could not be compared either.

topics.title: Overview of the API
topics.body:
SquatClient embeds Lua 5.1 as a sandboxed scripting language alongside the
[TinyFugue-style scripting language](help:scripting). Scripts are plain `.lua` files.

topics.title: Basics
topics.body:
- Everything lives in the global table `squat`. Each plugin gets its **own** global environment: globals you
  assign are private to your plugin, and changing `string`, `table` or `math` never affects other plugins.
- All scripts run on one thread, one at a time. You never need locks.
- Every call into your code (a trigger, a handler, a timer tick, loading the file) has a **budget**
  (about 5 million VM instructions and 500 ms wall-clock by default). Exceeding it aborts that call with an
  error in the log; the client keeps running and your other handlers still work.
- Errors in one plugin never stop another plugin.

## The `live` rule (important)

A line can be **live** (just arrived) or **replayed** (scrollback/backlog re-processed after reattaching).
Replayed lines only get *display effects*: `gag`, highlight colours, and spans returned by `line` handlers.
On replayed lines:

- trigger `fn` callbacks are **not called**;
- `line`/`prompt` handlers *are* called (with `l.live == false`) so they can restyle or gag, but
  `squat.send`, `echo`, `notify`, `tf`, `var.set`, `var.del`, `after`, `timer`, `on`, `trigger`, `alias` and
  `remove` do nothing and return `false`.

Write line handlers so they compute the display result from the text, and put side effects in trigger `fn`s.

topics.title: Sandbox
topics.body:
Available: base functions (`pairs`, `pcall`, `error`, `setmetatable`, `tostring`, `unpack` ...), `string`,
`table`, `math`, `coroutine`, and a restricted `os` with only `time`, `date`, `clock`, `difftime`
(using the client's clock). `print(...)` goes to the log.

Not available: `io`, `debug`, `package`, `os.execute/remove/rename/getenv/exit`, `dofile`, `loadfile`,
`string.dump`, `getfenv/setfenv`, `module`, `newproxy`, native modules. `loadstring`/`load` work but compile into your
own environment and refuse binary chunks. `string.rep` results are capped (4 MiB).

`require("name")` loads `name.lua` (dots become `/`) from **your plugin's own directory** only.

topics.title: Output and sending
topics.body:
| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `squat.send(text [, world])` | Send a line to the game. Returns `true`, or `nil, err`. |
| `squat.echo(x [, world])` | Show text locally. `x` is a string, one span `{s="..."}`, or an array of spans/strings. |
| `squat.notify(title [, body])` | Desktop notification. |
| `squat.log(text [, level])` | Write to the client log; level is `"info"`, `"warn"` or `"error"`. |
| `squat.world()` | Display name of the world the current line/event belongs to. |
| `squat.now()` | Seconds since the Unix epoch (float) from the client clock. |

`world` defaults to the world of the line/event being handled (timers remember the world they were created in).
Calling `send`/`echo`/`tf` with no current world and no `world` argument is an error.

## Spans and colours

A span is a table: `{s="text", fg=..., bg=..., b=true, dim=, i=, u=, st=, blink=, rev=, link="url"}`.

- `fg`/`bg` is an integer **0-255** (xterm-256 palette index; 0-15 follow the theme) or a string
  **`"#rrggbb"`** for 24-bit truecolor. Both survive the round trip to the display exactly; no quantisation.
- Anything else (`256`, `1.5`, `"red"`, `"#abc"`) is an error.

topics.title: Events: squat.on(event, fn [, priority])
topics.body:
| Event | `fn` receives |
|---|---|
| `line` | `{text, spans, world, prompt, live}` |
| `prompt` | the same, only for flushed prompts |
| `connect`, `disconnect` | `{world, ...}` (more fields depending on the event) |
| `gmcp` | `{package, data, raw, world}` (`data` is the decoded JSON) |
| `input` | `{text, world}`; return `true` to swallow the input |
| `timer` | a table describing the tick |

Line handlers may modify the line:

```lua
squat.on("line", function(l)
  if l.text:find("spam") then return {gag = true} end
  l.spans = {{s = "[!] ", fg = 196}, unpack(l.spans)}   -- assign a new table (in-place edits are not seen)
end)
```

Return `{gag=true}` to hide the line, `{spans=...}` to replace it, `{stop=true}` to stop later rules.
A gag does **not** stop later rules (so a gagged line can still trigger an auto-heal).

**Ordering:** triggers and `line` handlers form one list, run by `priority` (higher first, default 0), then in
registration order. This is deterministic and identical on live and replayed lines.

`squat.on` returns an id; `squat.remove(id)` (alias `squat.cancel`) unregisters it.

topics.title: Triggers and aliases
topics.body:
```lua
squat.trigger{
  match    = "You are hit by * for * damage.",  -- glob unless regex=true
  regex    = false,        -- true: RE2 regular expression (unanchored search)
  icase    = false,        -- case-insensitive
  gag      = false,        -- hide the line (display effect, also on replay)
  fg = "#ff8800", bg = 17, b = true, u = true,   -- highlight (display effect, also on replay)
  hilite   = "line",       -- "line" (default) or "match": colour only the matched text
  world    = "MyMUSH",     -- optional: only this world (name or id)
  priority = 0,
  fn       = function(m) ... end,   -- optional, live lines only
}
```

**Glob:** matches the whole line; `*` matches any run (captured), `?` one character, `\*` and `\?` are literal.
**Regex:** RE2 syntax (<https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax>): linear-time, no backreferences or
lookaround; named groups `(?P<name>...)`.

`fn(m)` gets `m.text`, `m[0]` (whole match), `m[1..n]` (captures; `""` if a group did not take part),
`m.named.<name>`, `m.world`, `m.live`, `m.spans`, `m.prompt`. It may return `{gag=true}`/`{spans=...}`/`{stop=true}`.

Aliases run on text the user typed:

```lua
squat.alias{match = "k *", fn = function(m) squat.send("kill " .. m[1]) end}
```

Same match options (`regex`, `icase`, `world`, `priority`). An alias handles the input (it is not sent) unless
its function returns `false`; the first handling alias wins.

topics.title: Timers
topics.body:
```lua
squat.timer{every = 30, count = 5, fn = function() ... end}   -- count omitted: repeat forever
squat.after(2.5, function() ... end)                          -- once
local id = squat.timer{...};  squat.cancel(id)
```

Intervals are seconds (minimum 0.05 by default, at most 512 live timers). Timers are removed on plugin reload. A tick that errors is logged and the timer keeps going.

topics.title: Variables
topics.body:
`squat.var.get(name [, default])`, `squat.var.set(name, value)`, `squat.var.del(name)`, `squat.var.keys()`.
Values are strings, numbers, booleans, or tables of those (JSON-compatible; functions and cycles are rejected).
`set(name, nil)` deletes. The store is shared by all plugins (prefix your names) and survives
`/reload`.

topics.title: Windows and panels: squat.ui
topics.body:
A script can open its own windows and docked panels in the SquatClient window. The runtime only keeps them as
data (the variable `ui.windows`); the client draws them, so they cost nothing in a client that has no window.
They belong to the script that opened them and disappear when it is unloaded (for a layout, when another
layout is chosen).

```lua
squat.ui.window{id = "who", title = "Who is online", x = 140, y = 90, w = 420,
  body = {type = "column", gap = 8, children = {
    {type = "table", columns = {{key = "name", title = "Name"}}, rows = {{name = "ann"}}},
    {type = "button", text = "Refresh", send = "/who"},
  }}}
squat.ui.panel{id = "trail", title = "Trail", dock = "right", body = {type = "text", value = "Limbo"}}
squat.ui.update("who", {title = "Who (3)"})     -- shallow merge into the spec
squat.ui.close("who");  squat.ui.list();  squat.ui.get("who")
```

`window` floats (the user drags it by the title bar and closes it with the ×; `open` is the same); `panel` docks
where a layout puts `<LuaPanels dock="right" />`. At most 32 at a time.

A `body` is a tree of nodes `{type = ..., children = {...}, ...props}`:
`column`, `row`, `grid` (`columns`), `panel` (`title`, `collapsible`, `open`), `tabs` (children with `title`),
`separator`, `heading` (`value`), `text` (`value`, `dim`, `bold`, `mono`, or `bind = "gmcp:Char.Vitals.hp"`),
`code` (`value`), `badge` (`value`, `tone` = ok|warn|danger), `button` (`text`, `send`, `tip`, `disabled`),
`table` (`columns`, `rows`, `empty`), `list` (`items`, `text`, `send` with `{name}`, `title`),
`gauge` (`value`, `max`, `label`, `color`), `input` (`placeholder`, `send` with `{value}`; Enter sends).
Unknown types draw nothing. Nothing in a spec is code: a button's `send` is text that goes through the normal
input pipeline, so a Lua alias can answer it (`send = "/who"` + `squat.alias{match = "/who", ...}`).

topics.title: Regular expressions
topics.body:
`squat.regex.match(pattern, text)` returns `nil` or a table `m[0]`, `m[1..n]`, `m.named`;
`squat.regex.test(pattern, text)` returns a boolean; `squat.regex.replace(pattern, text, repl)` uses `$1`/`${name}`.

topics.title: Talking to the TinyFugue-style language
topics.body:
`squat.tf(code [, world])` runs one line of TinyFugue-style input (`true` or `nil, err`).
Going the other way, the `/lua <code>` command runs Lua in a persistent console environment that keeps its
globals between commands.

topics.title: Plugins
topics.body:
```
plugins/
  heal.lua              a single-file plugin named "heal"
  combat/
    plugin.json         {"name": "combat", "version": "1.0", "description": "...", "enabled": true, "main": "main.lua"}
    main.lua            entry point (default main.lua, then init.lua)
    util.lua            require("util")
```

`plugin.json` is optional; `"enabled": false` skips the plugin. A plugin that fails to load is reported and skipped.
`/reload` discards all handlers, timers and plugin globals and re-runs every plugin from disk.

topics.title: Examples
topics.body:
Auto-heal:

```lua
squat.trigger{
  match = "^HP: (\\d+)/(\\d+)", regex = true,
  fn = function(m)
    local hp, max = tonumber(m[1]), tonumber(m[2])
    if hp / max < 0.4 and squat.now() - squat.var.get("last_heal", 0) > 3 then
      squat.var.set("last_heal", squat.now())
      squat.send("cast heal")
    end
  end,
}
```

Truecolor highlight:

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "*tells you*", fg = "#ff8800", b = true}
squat.trigger{match = "treasure", regex = true, hilite = "match", fg = "#ffd700", bg = 52}
```

Gag spam (still counting it on live lines):

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "^<Spam> ", regex = true, gag = true,
  fn = function() squat.var.set("spam_count", squat.var.get("spam_count", 0) + 1) end}
```

Timer (anti-idle, per connection):

```lua
squat.on("connect", function() squat.timer{every = 300, fn = function() squat.send("") end} end)
```

Alias:

```lua
squat.alias{match = "k *", fn = function(m) squat.send("kill " .. m[1]) end}
```

Call the TinyFugue-style language:

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "* arrives.", fn = function(m) squat.tf("/echo -aB Welcome, " .. m[1] .. "!") end}
```

topics.title: Limits (what the budget can and cannot stop)
topics.body:
Enforced per call: VM instruction count (main thread), wall-clock timeout (also stops coroutines), heap-growth
ceiling (sampled every 65536 instructions, process-wide so approximate), Lua call depth and stack size,
`string.rep` size, timer/variable counts. **Not** interruptible: a single long-running built-in such as a
pathological `string.find` pattern or very wide `string.format`; the call is marked failed when it returns, but it
can still occupy the (single) script thread until then. Prefer `squat.regex` (RE2, linear time) for untrusted patterns.
